title.zh: 卷二百下 列傳第一百五十下: 朱泚 黃巢 秦宗權
title.en: Volume 200 Biographies 150: Zhu Ci, Huang Chao, Qin Zongchuan
title.raw: 卷二百下 列傳第一百五十下: 朱泚 黃巢 秦宗權 Volume 200 Biographies 150: Zhu Ci, Huang Chao, Qin Zongchuan

sentences.zh: 朱泚黃巢秦宗權

translations.literal: Zhu Ci, Huang Chao, and Qin Zongquan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci, Huang Chao, and Qin Zongquan.

sentences.zh: 朱泚，幽州昌平人。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci was a man of Changping in Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was a native of Changping in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖利，贊善大夫，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Li was a Zanshan Dafu, posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Li had served as director of the crown prince's household; after death he was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 祖思明，太子洗馬，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: His grandfather Siming was crown prince groom, posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Siming had been groom of the heir apparent and was later posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 父懷珪，天寶初，事范陽節度使裴寬為衙前，授折沖將軍。

translations.literal: His father Huai Gui, at the beginning of the Tianbao era, served Fan-Yang military commissioner Pei Kuan as yamen runner and was appointed General of the Zhechong Army.
translations.idiomatic: His father Huai Gui, in the early Tianbao years, served under Fan-Yang military commissioner Pei Kuan as a yamen attendant and was appointed a general of the Zhechong army.

sentences.zh: 及安祿山、史思明叛，累為管兵將。

translations.literal: When An Lushan and Shi Siming rebelled, he repeatedly served as a commander of garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan and Shi Siming rose in rebellion, he served repeatedly as a commander of garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 寶應中，李懷仙歸順，奏為薊州刺史、平盧軍留後、柳城軍使。

translations.literal: In the Baoying era, when Li Huaixian submitted, he was memorialized as prefect of Ji, acting commissioner of the Pinglu army, and military commissioner of Liucheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoying reign, after Li Huaixian submitted to the court, Huai Gui was recommended as prefect of Ji, acting commissioner of the Pinglu army, and commander of the Liucheng garrison.

sentences.zh: 大曆元年卒，累贈左僕射。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of the Dali era and was posthumously promoted step by step to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in 766 and was posthumously promoted in stages to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 祖、父之贈，皆以泚故也。

translations.literal: The posthumous honors for grandfather and father were all because of Ci.
translations.idiomatic: The posthumous honors granted to his grandfather and father were all owing to Zhu Ci's position.

sentences.zh: 泚以父資從軍，幼壯偉，腰帶十圍，騎射武藝亦不出人。

translations.literal: Ci entered the army through his father's standing; in youth he was large and imposing, his belt ten arm-spans round, and in mounted archery and martial skill he was not below others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci entered the army through his father's standing. In his youth he was powerfully built, with a waist belt ten arm-spans around, and his horsemanship, archery, and martial skills were second to none.

sentences.zh: 外若寬和，中頗殘忍。

translations.literal: Outwardly he seemed mild and easy, inwardly he was quite cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he seemed mild and affable, but inwardly he was quite cruel.

sentences.zh: 然輕財好施，每征戰所得賞物，輒分與麾下將士，以是為眾所推，故得濟其凶謀。

translations.literal: Yet he was light with wealth and fond of giving; whenever he obtained rewards from campaigns he at once divided them among officers and soldiers under him, and thereby was pushed forward by the masses, so that he could accomplish his wicked designs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was generous with money and fond of giving. Whenever he received rewards from campaigning, he would at once share them among the officers and men under his command. For this he won the troops' esteem and was thus able to carry out his treacherous schemes.

sentences.zh: 初隸李懷仙為部將，改經略副使。

translations.literal: At first he was attached to Li Huaixian as a divisional commander, then was changed to deputy commissioner for frontier administration.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served under Li Huaixian as a divisional commander, and was later made deputy commissioner for frontier administration.

sentences.zh: 朱希彩既殺李懷仙，自為節度，以泚宗姓，甚委信之。

translations.literal: After Zhu Xicai had killed Li Huaixian and made himself military commissioner, because Ci shared the Zhu clan name he greatly entrusted and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhu Xicai killed Li Huaixian and made himself military commissioner, he placed great trust in Zhu Ci because they shared the Zhu clan name.

sentences.zh: 希彩為政苛酷，人不堪命。

translations.literal: Xicai's government was harsh and cruel, and the people could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: Xicai's rule was harsh and cruel, and the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 大曆七年秋，希彩為其下所殺，倉卒之際，未有所從。

translations.literal: In autumn of the seventh year of Dali, Xicai was killed by his subordinates; in the sudden emergency there was no one to follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of 772, Xicai was killed by his own men. In the sudden crisis, no leader had yet emerged.

sentences.zh: 泚營在城北，弟滔，主衙內兵，亦得眾心。

translations.literal: Ci's camp was north of the city; his younger brother Tao commanded the inner-garrison troops and also won the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's camp lay north of the city. His younger brother Tao commanded the inner-garrison troops and likewise won the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 滔變詐多端，潛使百餘人於眾中大言曰：「節度使非城北朱副使莫可。」

translations.literal: Tao was changeable and deceitful in many ways; secretly he sent more than a hundred men to proclaim loudly among the crowd: "For military commissioner none but Vice Commissioner Zhu north of the city will do."
translations.idiomatic: Tao was shrewd and full of shifting schemes. He secretly sent more than a hundred men to shout among the troops: "No one but Vice Commissioner Zhu north of the city is fit to be military commissioner."

sentences.zh: 眾既無從，因共推泚。

translations.literal: The crowd having no one else to follow, thereupon jointly pushed Ci forward.
translations.idiomatic: With no other candidate at hand, the men jointly acclaimed Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 泚遂權知留後，遣使奉表京師。

translations.literal: Ci thereupon acted as acting military commissioner, and sent envoys to present a memorial to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci thereupon assumed acting command as military commissioner and sent envoys to present a memorial to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，拜檢校左散騎常侍、兼御史中丞、幽州盧龍節度等使、幽州長史、兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he was appointed acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong and related posts, Youzhou chief administrator, and concurrently Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was appointed acting Left Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, chief administrator of Youzhou, and concurrently Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 其年，泚上表令弟滔率兵二千五百人赴京西防秋。

translations.literal: That year Ci memorialized requesting that his younger brother Tao lead twenty-five hundred troops west to the capital for autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Zhu Ci memorialized the throne, asking that his younger brother Tao lead twenty-five hundred troops to the western capital for autumn defense.

sentences.zh: 代宗嘉之，手詔褒美。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong commended this and personally issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong commended this and issued a personal edict in praise.

sentences.zh: 九年，就加檢校戶部尚書，賜實封百戶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was further appointed acting Minister of Revenue and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was further appointed acting Minister of Revenue and granted a substantive fief of one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 幽州及河北諸鎮，自天寶末便為逆亂之地，李懷仙、朱希彩與連境三節度，名雖向順，未嘗朝謁。

translations.literal: Youzhou and the Hebei circuits from the end of Tianbao had been lands of rebellion; Li Huaixian, Zhu Xicai, and the three military commissioners of the adjoining circuits, though nominally submissive, had never come to court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhou and the other Hebei circuits had been hotbeds of rebellion since the late Tianbao years. Li Huaixian, Zhu Xicai, and the three neighboring military commissioners had submitted in name only and had never once presented themselves at court.

sentences.zh: 至是泚率先上表，請自領步騎三千人入覲，詔修甲第以待之。

translations.literal: At this time Ci was the first to memorialize, asking to lead three thousand infantry and cavalry himself to attend court; an edict ordered a fine mansion prepared to await him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Zhu Ci was the first to memorialize, asking to lead three thousand foot and horse troops in person to attend court. The emperor ordered a fine mansion prepared to receive him.

sentences.zh: 九月，泚至京師，代宗禦內殿引見，賜御馬兩匹、戰馬十匹、金銀錦彩甚厚。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Ci arrived at the capital; Daizong received him in audience in the inner hall and bestowed two imperial horses, ten war horses, and very generous gold, silver, and brocades.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Zhu Ci reached the capital. Daizong received him in audience in the inner palace and bestowed two imperial horses, ten war horses, and lavish gifts of gold, silver, and brocades.

sentences.zh: 又以器物十床、馬四十匹、絹二萬匹、衣一千七百襲賜其將士，宴犒之盛，近時未有。

translations.literal: He also bestowed on his officers and soldiers ten sets of utensils, forty horses, twenty thousand bolts of silk, and seventeen hundred suits of clothing; the scale of the feast and rewards had not been seen in recent times.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave his officers and men ten sets of utensils, forty horses, twenty thousand bolts of silk, and seventeen hundred suits of clothing. The scale of the feast and rewards was unprecedented in recent memory.

sentences.zh: 泚又上表，請留京師，從之。

translations.literal: Ci again memorialized asking to remain at the capital, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci memorialized again, asking to remain at the capital, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 因授其弟滔兼御史大夫、幽州節度留後。

translations.literal: Thereupon his younger brother Tao was appointed concurrently Grand Censor and acting military commissioner of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tao was then appointed concurrently Grand Censor and acting military commissioner of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 仍以河陽永平軍防秋兵，郭子儀統之；

translations.literal: The autumn-defense troops of the Heyang and Yongping armies were still placed under Guo Ziyi's command;
translations.idiomatic: The autumn-defense troops of the Heyang and Yongping armies remained under Guo Ziyi's command;

sentences.zh: 決勝軍楊猷兵，李抱玉統之；

translations.literal: the troops of Yang You of the Juesheng Army were commanded by Li Baoyu;
translations.idiomatic: the troops of Yang You's Juesheng army were commanded by Li Baoyu;

sentences.zh: 淮西鳳翔兵，馬璘統之；

translations.literal: the Huai-Xi and Fengxiang troops were commanded by Ma Lin;
translations.idiomatic: the Huai-Xi and Fengxiang troops were commanded by Ma Lin;

sentences.zh: 汴宋、淄青兵，俾泚統焉。

translations.literal: the Bian-Song and Zi-Qing troops were made subject to Ci's command.
translations.idiomatic: and the Bian-Song and Zi-Qing troops were placed under Zhu Ci's command.

sentences.zh: 十一年八月，加拜同平章事。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the eleventh year he was further appointed Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the eleventh year he was further appointed associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 尋令出鎮奉天行營，復賜金銀繒彩並內庫弓箭以寵之。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered out to take command of the Fengtian field headquarters, and again was bestowed gold, silver, silks, and bows and arrows from the inner treasury as marks of favor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered out to command the Fengtian field headquarters, and was again showered with gold, silver, silks, and bows and arrows from the inner treasury as marks of imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加檢校司空，代李抱玉為隴右節度使，權知河西、澤潞行營兵馬事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was further appointed acting Minister of Works, replacing Li Baoyu as military commissioner of Longyou and acting in charge of the Hexi and Zelu field headquarters' military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was further appointed acting Minister of Works, replacing Li Baoyu as military commissioner of Longyou and placed in charge of the Hexi and Zelu field armies.

sentences.zh: 德宗嗣位，加太子太師、鳳翔尹，實封至三百戶。

translations.literal: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Ci was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Fengxiang, and his substantive fief was raised to three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong succeeded to the throne, Zhu Ci was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and prefect of Fengxiang, and his substantive fief was increased to three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 建中元年，涇州將劉文喜阻兵為亂，加泚四鎮北庭行軍、涇原節度使，與諸軍討之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianzhong, Jingzhou general Liu Wenxi blocked the army and made rebellion; Ci was made commander of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign and military commissioner of Jingyuan, and with the various armies punished him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianzhong, Jingzhou general Liu Wenxi mutinied and rebelled. Zhu Ci was made commander of the Four Garrisons and Beiting campaign and military commissioner of Jingyuan, and led the allied armies against him.

sentences.zh: 涇州平，加泚中書令，還鎮鳳翔，而以舒王讓遙領涇原節度。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou was pacified, Ci was made Grand Secretariat Director, returned to garrison Fengxiang, and Prince Shu Li Rang was made titular military commissioner of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingzhou was pacified, Zhu Ci was made Grand Secretariat Director and returned to garrison Fengxiang, while Prince Shu Li Rang was given nominal command of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 二年，加泚太尉。

translations.literal: In the second year Ci was made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zhu Ci was made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 朱滔將反叛，陰使人與泚計議，以帛書納蠟丸中，置髮髻間。

translations.literal: Zhu Tao was about to rebel; secretly he sent a man to consult with Ci, placing a silk letter inside a wax pellet and hiding it in his hair bun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Tao was plotting rebellion and secretly sent a messenger to consult with Zhu Ci, concealing a silk letter inside a wax pellet hidden in the messenger's hair bun.

sentences.zh: 河東節度馬燧搜獲之，以聞，並送帛書及所遣使。

translations.literal: Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui searched and seized it, reported to the throne, and sent up both the silk letter and the envoy dispatched.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong military commissioner Ma Sui seized the messenger, reported to the throne, and forwarded both the silk letter and the envoy.

sentences.zh: 泚惶懼，頓首乞歸罪有司。

translations.literal: Ci was fearful and in panic, bowing his head and begging to surrender himself to the authorities for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was terrified and prostrated himself, begging to surrender himself to the authorities for judgment.

sentences.zh: 上勉之曰：「千里不同謀，非卿之過。」

translations.literal: The emperor comforted him, saying: "A thousand li apart, you did not plot together—this is not your fault."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor reassured him: "You were a thousand li apart and did not plot together—this is not your fault."

sentences.zh: 三年四月，以張鎰代泚為鳳翔隴右節度留後，留泚京師，加實封至一千戶，與一子正員官，其幽州盧龍節度、太尉、中書令並如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang Yi replaced Ci as acting military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou; Ci was kept at the capital, his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and one son was given a regular official post; his posts as military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Secretariat Director remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year Zhang Yi replaced Zhu Ci as acting military commissioner of Fengxiang and Longyou. Zhu Ci was kept at the capital, his substantive fief was raised to one thousand households, and one of his sons was given a regular official post; his titles as military commissioner of Youzhou and Lulong, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Secretariat Director remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 四年十月，涇原兵叛，鑾駕幸奉天。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year the Jingyuan troops rebelled, and the imperial carriage went to Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year the Jingyuan troops mutinied, and the emperor fled to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 叛卒等以泚嘗統涇州，知其失權廢居，怏怏思亂。

translations.literal: The rebel soldiers and others, because Ci had once commanded Jingzhou, knew he had lost power and lived in retirement, resentful and thinking of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The mutineers knew that Zhu Ci had once commanded Jingzhou and that he now lived in forced retirement, stripped of power and brooding over his grievances.

sentences.zh: 群寇無帥，幸泚政寬，乃相與謀曰：「朱太尉久囚空宅，若迎而為主，事必濟矣！」

translations.literal: The band of rebels had no leader; fortunately Ci's rule was lenient, and they therefore plotted together, saying: "Grand Preceptor Zhu has long been confined in an empty residence—if we welcome him and make him lord, the affair will surely succeed!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had no leader, and Zhu Ci's reputation for leniency gave them hope. They plotted together: "Grand Preceptor Zhu has long been confined in an empty mansion—if we welcome him as our leader, we are sure to succeed!"

sentences.zh: 姚令言乃率百餘騎迎泚于晉昌里第。

translations.literal: Yao Lingyan thereupon led more than a hundred horsemen to welcome Ci at his residence in Jinchang Ward.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan then led more than a hundred horsemen to fetch Zhu Ci from his residence in Jinchang Ward.

sentences.zh: 泚乘馬擁從北向，燭炬星羅，觀者萬計，入居含元殿。

translations.literal: Ci mounted his horse with a crowded escort heading north; torches were strewn like stars, onlookers numbered in the tens of thousands, and he entered and dwelt in the Hanyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci rode northward with a great escort, torches blazing like a field of stars and tens of thousands looking on. He entered and took up residence in the Hanyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 明日，移處白華殿，但稱太尉。

translations.literal: The next day he moved to the Baihua Hall and was addressed only as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he moved to the Baihua Hall and was addressed only as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 朝官有謁泚者，悉勸奉迎鑾駕，既不合泚意，皆逡巡而退。

translations.literal: Court officials who came to call on Ci all urged welcoming back the imperial carriage; this did not suit Ci's intent, and they all hesitated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials who came to see Zhu Ci all urged him to welcome the emperor back. This did not suit his plans, and they all withdrew in hesitation.

sentences.zh: 源休至，遂屏人移時，言多悖逆。

translations.literal: When Yuan Xiu arrived, he dismissed attendants and spoke at length; his words were mostly rebellious.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Xiu arrived, he dismissed the attendants and spoke at length, his words for the most part treasonous.

sentences.zh: 又盛陳成敗，稱述符命，勸其僭偽，泚甚悅之。

translations.literal: He also set forth success and failure at length, cited portents and mandates, and urged usurpation; Ci was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He also expounded at length on success and failure, cited omens and heavenly mandates, and urged Zhu Ci to usurp the throne. Zhu Ci was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 又李忠臣、張光晟繼至，咸以官閑積憤，樂於禍亂。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchen and Zhang Guangcheng also arrived in succession; all, because their offices were idle and grievances had accumulated, rejoiced in calamity and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen and Zhang Guangcheng also arrived in turn. All of them, idle in office and nursing old resentments, welcomed the chaos.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔涇原大將張廷芝、段誠諫以潰卒三千餘自襄城而至。

translations.literal: The Fengxiang and Jingyuan generals Zhang Tingzhi and Duan Chengjian came from Xiangcheng with more than three thousand routed soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: The Fengxiang and Jingyuan generals Zhang Tingzhi and Duan Chengjian arrived from Xiangcheng with more than three thousand routed troops.

sentences.zh: 賊泚自謂眾望所集，僭竊之心，自此而定。

translations.literal: The rebel Ci considered himself the focus of popular expectation, and his heart to usurp was from this time fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Zhu Ci believed himself the focus of universal acclaim, and from that moment his resolve to seize the throne was fixed.

sentences.zh: 乃以源休為京兆尹、判度支，李忠臣為皇城使。

translations.literal: He thereupon made Yuan Xiu metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and controller of the treasury, and Li Zhongchen commissioner of the imperial city.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Yuan Xiu metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and controller of the treasury, and Li Zhongchen commissioner of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 須秀實久失兵柄，故推心委之。

translations.literal: Xu Xiushi had long lost military authority, and therefore Ci entrusted him with full confidence.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shishi had long been stripped of military command, and Zhu Ci therefore placed full trust in him.

sentences.zh: 遂發銳師三千，言奉迎乘輿，實陰有逆謀。

translations.literal: He thereupon sent out three thousand crack troops, saying they were to welcome the imperial carriage, but in fact harboring a secret design of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He then dispatched three thousand elite troops, claiming they were to welcome the emperor, but in fact plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 秀實與劉海賓謀誅泚，且虞叛卒之震驚法駕，乃潛為賊符，追所發兵。

translations.literal: Xiushi and Liu Haibin plotted to kill Ci; moreover, fearing the rebel soldiers would alarm the imperial carriage, he secretly forged a rebel tally and recalled the troops sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shishi and Liu Haibin plotted to assassinate Zhu Ci. Fearing the mutineers might alarm the emperor, Shishi secretly forged a rebel tally and recalled the dispatched troops.

sentences.zh: 至六日，兵及駱驛而回。

translations.literal: By the sixth day the troops reached Luoyi Post and returned.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth day the troops had reached Luoyi Post and turned back.

sentences.zh: 因與海賓同入見泚，為陳逆順之理，而海賓於靴中取匕首，為其所覺，遂不得前。

translations.literal: Thereupon he and Haibin together entered to see Ci and set forth the logic of rebellion and loyalty; but Haibin drew a dagger from his boot, was detected, and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Shishi and Haibin then went in together to see Zhu Ci and argued the rights of loyalty and treason. Haibin drew a dagger from his boot, but Zhu Ci detected it and he could not strike.

sentences.zh: 秀實知不可以義動，遽奪源休象笏，挺而擊泚，仍大呼曰：「反虜萬段！」

translations.literal: Xiushi knew he could not move Ci by righteousness; he abruptly seized Yuan Xiu's ivory tablet, drew it forth and struck Ci, and still shouted loudly: "Traitor rebel, ten thousand pieces!"
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he could not sway Zhu Ci by argument, Shishi snatched Yuan Xiu's ivory tablet and struck Zhu Ci with it, shouting, "Traitor! May you be cut to ten thousand pieces!"

sentences.zh: 泚舉臂衛首，秀實格拉之，忷々然。

translations.literal: Ci raised his arm to guard his head; Xiushi seized and pulled him, in a furious struggle.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci raised his arm to shield his head. Shishi seized him and they grappled furiously.

sentences.zh: 李忠臣馳肋泚，泚素多力，才破其面，逆徒噪集，秀實、海賓遂並見害。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchen rushed to assist Ci; Ci had always been very strong and had only just broken Xiushi's face when the rebel mob clamored and gathered—Xiushi and Haibin were thereupon both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen rushed to Zhu Ci's aid. Zhu Ci had always been exceptionally strong and had only just bloodied Shishi's face when the rebels swarmed in. Shishi and Haibin were both killed.

sentences.zh: 十日，泚自領兵侵逼奉天，竊威儀輦輅，闐溢道途，蟻聚之眾軍勢頗盛；

translations.literal: On the tenth day Ci personally led troops to press Fengtian, usurping imperial regalia and carriages; the roads were packed full, and the ant-like mass of troops was quite strong in military force;
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth day Zhu Ci personally led his army against Fengtian, usurping imperial regalia and carriages. The roads were choked with men, and his swarm of troops made a formidable host;

sentences.zh: 以姚令言為元帥，張光晟為副。

translations.literal: Yao Lingyan was made commander-in-chief and Zhang Guangcheng deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan was made commander-in-chief and Zhang Guangcheng his deputy.

sentences.zh: 以李忠臣為京兆尹、皇城留守，居中書省。

translations.literal: Li Zhongchen was made metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and commissioner in charge of the imperial city, residing in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhongchen was made metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao and commissioner in charge of the imperial city, with his office in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 尋以蔣鎮為門下侍郎，李子平為諫議大夫兼平章事。

translations.literal: Soon Jiang Zhen was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Li Ziping Remonstrance Grandee concurrently Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jiang Zhen was made Vice Director of the Chancellery and Li Ziping Remonstrance Grandee and associate grand councilor.

sentences.zh: 泚軍合於城下，渾瑊、韓遊瑰禦之，泚眾大敗，死者萬計。

translations.literal: Ci's army gathered below the city; Hun Jian and Han Yougui defended against them, and Ci's masses were greatly defeated, the dead numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's army massed below the city. Hun Jian and Han Yougui defended it, and Zhu Ci's forces were routed with tens of thousands dead.

sentences.zh: 泚收軍於奉天東三里下營，大修攻具。

translations.literal: Ci gathered his army three li east of Fengtian and encamped, greatly repairing siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci withdrew three li east of Fengtian and encamped, throwing himself into building siege engines.

sentences.zh: 明日，泚又分兵營於乾陵下瞰，城內大震。

translations.literal: The next day Ci again divided troops to encamp below Qianling and look down on the city; within the city there was great alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhu Ci sent detachments to camp below Qianling and overlook the city, throwing the defenders into great alarm.

sentences.zh: 十一月三日，杜希全與泚眾戰于漠穀，官軍不利，自是泚益驕大。

translations.literal: On the third day of the eleventh month Du Xiquan fought Ci's masses at Mogu Valley; the imperial army was unfavorable, and from this time Ci grew ever more arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: On the third day of the eleventh month Du Xiquan fought Zhu Ci's troops at Mogu Valley. The imperial army fared badly, and from then on Zhu Ci grew ever more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 王師乘城而戰，人百其勇，賊多敗恤。

translations.literal: The imperial army fought from atop the walls; each man showed a hundredfold courage, and the rebels mostly suffered defeat and distress.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial troops fought from the walls, each man fighting with redoubled courage, and the rebels suffered repeated defeats.

sentences.zh: 或出野戰，官軍又獲利焉。

translations.literal: Sometimes they went out for field battle, and the imperial army again gained advantage.
translations.idiomatic: When they sallied out for field battle, the imperial army again gained the upper hand.

sentences.zh: 泚乃大驅百姓填塹，夜攻城，城中設奇以應之，賊乃退縮。

translations.literal: Ci thereupon drove the common people in great numbers to fill the moat, attacking the city by night; within the city stratagems were set to meet this, and the rebels then drew back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci then drove masses of civilians to fill the moat and attacked the city by night. The defenders met him with counter-stratagems, and the rebels fell back.

sentences.zh: 西明寺僧法堅有巧思，為泚造雲梯。

translations.literal: The monk Fajian of Ximing Temple had clever ingenuity and built a cloud-ladder for Ci.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Fajian of Ximing Temple, a man of ingenious mind, built a siege tower for Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 十五日辰時，梯臨城東北隅，城內震駭。

translations.literal: At the chen hour on the fifteenth day the ladder reached the northeast corner of the city wall, and within the city there was shock and terror.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch on the fifteenth day the tower reached the northeast corner of the wall, throwing the city into terror.

sentences.zh: 渾瑊使侯仲莊設大坑，為地道陷之。

translations.literal: Hun Jian had Hou Zhongzhuang set a great pit and made an underground passage to cause it to collapse.
translations.idiomatic: Hun Jian had Hou Zhongzhuang dig a great pit and a tunnel to undermine it.

sentences.zh: 又縱火焚其梯，東風起，吹我軍，眾頗危。

translations.literal: He also set fire to burn the ladder; an east wind rose and blew toward our army, and the masses were quite imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: They also set fire to the tower. An east wind rose and blew toward the imperial troops, putting them in grave danger.

sentences.zh: 俄而風回，吹賊軍，瑊益薪潑油，萬鼓齊震，風吹俱熾，須臾雲梯與凶黨同為灰燼。

translations.literal: Soon the wind turned back and blew toward the rebel army; Jian added fuel and poured oil, ten thousand drums sounded together, the wind blew and all blazed fiercely, and in a moment the cloud-ladder and the wicked band were alike ashes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the wind shifted and blew toward the rebels. Jian piled on fuel and oil, ten thousand drums thundered together, and the flames leaped up. In a moment the siege tower and the rebels upon it were reduced to ash.

sentences.zh: 城中三門悉出兵，王師又捷，其夜兵復出攻，泚眾敗績。

translations.literal: From three gates within the city troops all went out; the imperial army again won victory, and that night the army again went out to attack and Ci's masses were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops sallied from all three gates and won another victory. That night they attacked again, and Zhu Ci's forces were routed.

sentences.zh: 李懷光以五萬人來援，自河北至，泚眾惶駭，因而大潰，長圍遂解焉。

translations.literal: Li Huai Guang came to aid with fifty thousand men from Hebei; Ci's masses were fearful and alarmed and thereby greatly routed, and the long siege was thereupon lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huai Guang arrived from Hebei with fifty thousand reinforcements. Zhu Ci's army panicked, broke, and fled, and the long siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 眾庶以懷光三日不至，城則危矣。

translations.literal: The common people considered that if Huai Guang did not arrive within three days, the city would be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: The people believed that if Huai Guang did not arrive within three days, the city would be lost.

sentences.zh: 三十日夜，泚走至京城。

translations.literal: On the night of the thirtieth day Ci fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the thirtieth Zhu Ci fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時姚令言於城中造戰格拋樓，每坊團結，人心大異。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Lingyan within the city built fighting towers and catapult platforms, and each ward was organized into groups; people's hearts were greatly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan was building fighting towers and catapult platforms in the city and organizing each ward into militia units, and morale among the people shifted sharply.

sentences.zh: 泚自奉天回，乃悉令去之，曰：「攻戰吾自有計。」

translations.literal: When Ci returned from Fengtian he ordered all of these removed, saying: "For attack and battle I have my own plans."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci returned from Fengtian he ordered them all dismantled, saying, "I have my own plans for assault."

sentences.zh: 前此每三五日，即使人偽自城外來，周走號令曰：「奉天已破！」

translations.literal: Before this, every three or five days he would send men pretending to come from outside the city, who would walk about crying orders: "Fengtian has fallen!"
translations.idiomatic: Every few days he had men pretend to arrive from outside the city, running through the streets shouting, "Fengtian has fallen!"

sentences.zh: 百姓聞之，莫不飲泣，道路闃寂。

translations.literal: When the common people heard this, none failed to weep; the roads were silent and deserted.
translations.idiomatic: The people wept at the news, and the streets fell silent and deserted.

sentences.zh: 時有入臺省吏人，不過十數輩，郎官六七人，而亦令依常年舉選，初有數十人陳狀，旬日亦皆摒退。

translations.literal: At the time there were clerks entering the Censorate and Secretariat, no more than a dozen-odd, and six or seven court gentlemen; yet he also ordered the regular annual selection to proceed—at first several dozen men submitted petitions, but within ten days all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Only a dozen or so clerks and six or seven court gentlemen still attended the Censorate and Secretariat, yet Zhu Ci still ordered the regular civil-service selection to proceed. Several dozen men submitted petitions at first, but within ten days all were turned away.

sentences.zh: 泚自號其宅曰潛龍宮，悉移內庫珍貨瑰寶以實之。

translations.literal: Ci himself styled his residence the Palace of the Hidden Dragon and moved all the rare goods and precious treasures of the inner treasury to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci named his residence the Palace of the Hidden Dragon and filled it with treasures from the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 識者曰：「《易》稱『潛龍勿用』，此敗徵也。」

translations.literal: Those with insight said: "The Changes says 'the hidden dragon—do not employ it'; this is a sign of defeat."
translations.idiomatic: The knowing said, "The Book of Changes says, 'The hidden dragon—do not act.' This is an omen of defeat."

sentences.zh: 無幾，百姓剽奪其珍寶，泚不能禁止。

translations.literal: Before long the common people plundered his treasures, and Ci could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the people looted his treasures, and Zhu Ci could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 明年正月一日，泚改偽國號曰漢，稱天皇元年。

translations.literal: On the first day of the first month of the following year Ci changed his false state designation to Han and proclaimed the first year of the Heavenly Sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the new year Zhu Ci changed his rebel state name to Han and proclaimed the first year of the Heavenly Sovereign.

sentences.zh: 二月，李懷光既圖叛逆，遣使與泚通和。

translations.literal: In the second month, when Li Huai Guang had already plotted rebellion, he sent envoys to treat with Ci.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, after Li Huai Guang had turned rebel, he sent envoys to negotiate an alliance with Zhu Ci.

sentences.zh: 鑾駕幸梁、洋，自此衣冠之潛匿者，出受偽官十七八焉。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage went to Liang and Yang; from this time those in official dress who had hidden themselves came forth and accepted false offices, seven or eight out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fled to Liang and Yang. From then on, seven or eight out of ten officials who had been in hiding came forward to accept posts under the rebel regime.

sentences.zh: 懷光初與泚往復通好甚密，以錢谷金帛互相饋遺。

translations.literal: At first Huai Guang and Ci exchanged courtesies back and forth very closely, presenting money, grain, gold, and silks to one another.
translations.idiomatic: At first Huai Guang and Zhu Ci maintained a close correspondence, exchanging money, grain, gold, and silks as gifts.

sentences.zh: 泚與書，事之如兄，約云：「削平關中，當割據山河，永為鄰國。」

translations.literal: Ci wrote to him, treating him as an elder brother, and agreed, saying: "When Guanzhong is pacified, we shall each hold the mountains and rivers in partition and be neighboring states forever.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci wrote to him as to an elder brother and pledged: "When we have pacified Guanzhong, we shall divide the realm between us and remain neighboring states forever.

sentences.zh: 及懷光決計背叛，逼乘輿遷幸，泚乃下偽詔書，待懷光以臣禮，仍徵兵馬。

translations.literal: When Huai Guang had resolved on rebellion and forced the imperial carriage to relocate, Zhu Ci then issued a false edict, treating Huai Guang with the rites due a subject, and also requisitioned troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Once Li Huai Guang had made up his mind to rebel and forced the emperor to flee the capital, Zhu Ci issued a forged imperial edict addressing Huai Guang as a loyal subject and calling up his armies.

sentences.zh: 懷光既為所賣，慚怒憤恥，遂領眾遁歸河中。

translations.literal: Huai Guang, having been betrayed, felt shame, rage, indignation, and disgrace, and then led his followers in flight back to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Betrayed and consumed by shame and fury, Li Huai Guang withdrew with his army to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 三月，李晟、駱元光、尚可孤之眾，悉於城東累敗泚眾。

translations.literal: In the third month, the forces of Li Sheng, Luo Yuanguang, and Shang Ke'gu all repeatedly defeated Zhu Ci's troops east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, east of the city, the armies of Li Sheng, Luo Yuanguang, and Shang Ke'gu inflicted a series of defeats on Zhu Ci's forces.

sentences.zh: 四月，泚使韓旻、宋歸朝、張庭芝等寇武功，渾瑊以眾及吐蕃論莽羅大敗歸朝，殺逆党萬餘人于武亭川。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, Zhu Ci sent Han Min, Song Guichao, Zhang Tingzhi, and others to raid Wugong; Hun Jian with his troops, together with the Tibetan Lun Mangluo, greatly defeated Guichao and killed more than ten thousand rebels at Wuting Stream.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Zhu Ci dispatched Han Min, Song Guichao, and Zhang Tingzhi against Wugong. Hun Jian, reinforced by the Tibetan chieftain Lun Mangluo, routed Song Guichao's column and slaughtered more than ten thousand rebels at Wuting Stream.

sentences.zh: 五月，泚又使仇敬忠寇藍田，尚可孤擊之，大破泚眾，擒敬忠斬之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Zhu Ci again sent Qiu Jingzhong to raid Lantian; Shang Ke'gu attacked him, greatly defeated Zhu Ci's troops, captured Jingzhong, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zhu Ci sent Qiu Jingzhong against Lantian. Shang Ke'gu struck back, shattered the rebel army, captured Jingzhong, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 李晟、駱元光、尚可孤遂悉師齊進，晟屯光泰門，逆徒拒官軍，王師累捷。

translations.literal: Li Sheng, Luo Yuanguang, and Shang Ke'gu then advanced together with all their armies; Li Sheng encamped at Guangtai Gate; the rebels resisted the imperial army, and the royal troops repeatedly won victories.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sheng, Luo Yuanguang, and Shang Ke'gu then marched in full strength. Li Sheng took position at Guangtai Gate. Though the rebels stood firm against the imperial columns, the government armies won victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 二十八日，官軍入苑，收復京師，逆黨大潰。

translations.literal: On the twenty-eighth day, the imperial army entered the imperial park, recovered the capital, and the rebels fled in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-eighth the imperial forces entered the palace grounds, retook the capital, and the rebel host collapsed in flight.

sentences.zh: 泚與姚令言、張庭芝、源休、李子平、朱遂以數千人西走，其餘黨或奔竄，或來降。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci, together with Yao Lingyan, Zhang Tingzhi, Yuan Xiu, Li Ziping, and Zhu Su, fled west with several thousand men; the remaining rebels either scattered in flight or came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci fled west with Yao Lingyan, Zhang Tingzhi, Yuan Xiu, Li Ziping, and Zhu Su and a few thousand men, while the rest of the rebels either scattered or surrendered.

sentences.zh: 泚眾緣路潰散，乃奔涇州，才百餘騎。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's followers scattered along the road in defeat; he fled to Jing Prefecture with only a little more than a hundred horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's force melted away along the road until he reached Jing Prefecture with barely a hundred riders left.

sentences.zh: 田希鑒閉門登陴，泚令謂鑒曰：「我與爾節度，何故背恩？」

translations.literal: Tian Xijian shut the gates and mounted the walls; Zhu Ci had someone say to Xijian: "I gave you the military governorship—why have you betrayed my kindness?
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xijian barred the gates and manned the walls. Zhu Ci sent a messenger to demand: "I made you military governor—why have you turned against me?

sentences.zh: 希鑒乃使人自城上擲泚所送旌節于外，續又投火焚之。

translations.literal: Xijian then had men throw from atop the wall the banner and credentials Zhu Ci had sent him, and afterward cast them into fire and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Xijian had his men hurl the banner of command and commission Zhu Ci had bestowed on him down from the ramparts, then set them ablaze.

sentences.zh: 泚遂過數里，息於逆旅。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci then went several li farther and rested at an inn.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci rode on a few li further and stopped to rest at a roadside inn.

sentences.zh: 泚將梁庭芬入涇州說田希鑒曰：「公比日殺馮河清背叛，今雖歸順，國家必不能久容，公他日不免受禍。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's general Liang Tingfen entered Jing Prefecture and said to Tian Xijian: "You recently killed Feng Heqing for rebellion; though you have now submitted, the state surely cannot long tolerate you—you will someday not escape calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's officer Liang Tingfen entered Jing Prefecture and urged Tian Xijian: "You killed Feng Heqing for turning rebel. Even if you have submitted now, the court will never trust you for long. Sooner or later disaster will find you.

sentences.zh: 何如開門納朱公，與共成大事！」

translations.literal: Why not open the gates and admit Lord Zhu, and together accomplish a great enterprise!
translations.idiomatic: Better to open the gates, welcome Lord Zhu, and join him in a great undertaking!

sentences.zh: 希鑒以為然。

translations.literal: Xijian thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xijian agreed.

sentences.zh: 庭芬乃追及泚言之，泚大悅，使庭芬卻往涇州。

translations.literal: Tingfen then caught up with Zhu Ci and told him this; Zhu Ci was greatly pleased and sent Tingfen back to Jing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tingfen rode after Zhu Ci with the news. Delighted, Zhu Ci sent him back to Jing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庭芬請授己尚書、平章事，泚不從。

translations.literal: Tingfen requested that he himself be granted the posts of Minister and Grand Councilor; Zhu Ci did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Tingfen asked to be made Minister and Grand Councilor. Zhu Ci refused.

sentences.zh: 梁庭芬既求宰相不得，不復往涇州，從泚至甯州彭原縣西城屯，復與泚心腹朱惟孝共射泚。

translations.literal: Liang Tingfen, having failed to obtain the chancellorship, no longer went to Jing Prefecture; he followed Zhu Ci to the western camp at Pengyuan County in Ning Prefecture, and again together with Zhu Ci's confidant Zhu Weixiao jointly shot at Zhu Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Denied the chancellorship, Liang Tingfen abandoned the mission to Jing Prefecture and stayed with Zhu Ci as far as the western camp at Pengyuan in Ning Prefecture, where he and Zhu Ci's trusted follower Zhu Weixiao opened fire on him together.

sentences.zh: 泚走，墜故窖中。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci fled and fell into an old cellar.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci bolted and tumbled into an abandoned pit.

sentences.zh: 泚左右韓旻、薛綸、高幽嵓、武震、朱進卿、董希芝共斬泚，使宋膺傳首以獻。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's attendants Han Min, Xue Lun, Gao Youyan, Wu Zhen, Zhu Jinqing, and Dong Xizhi together beheaded Zhu Ci and sent Song Ying to carry the head as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Han Min, Xue Lun, Gao Youyan, Wu Zhen, Zhu Jinqing, and Dong Xizhi, Zhu Ci's own followers, cut off his head and dispatched Song Ying to present it to the court.

sentences.zh: 泚死時年四十三。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci died he was forty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci was forty-three at his death.

sentences.zh: 姚令言投涇州，源休、李子平走鳳翔，尋並斬獲。

translations.literal: Yao Lingyan fled to Jing Prefecture; Yuan Xiu and Li Ziping fled to Fengxiang—they were soon all captured and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan fled toward Jing Prefecture; Yuan Xiu and Li Ziping fled to Fengxiang. All were soon captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 宋歸朝之敗武功，降于李懷光，送興元斬之。

translations.literal: Song Guichao, defeated at Wugong, surrendered to Li Huai Guang and was sent to Xingyuan, where he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeat at Wugong, Song Guichao surrendered to Li Huai Guang and was sent to Xingyuan for execution.

sentences.zh: 唯不獲朱遂，傳為野人所殺，或云與泚婿偽金吾將軍馬悅潛走党項部落，數月得達幽州。

translations.literal: Only Zhu Su was not captured; it is reported that wild tribesmen killed him, or some say that he secretly fled with Zhu Ci's son-in-law, the false Jinwu General Ma Yue, to a Tangut tribe, reaching You Prefecture after several months.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zhu Su escaped capture. Some said hill tribes killed him; others said he fled in secret with Zhu Ci's son-in-law, the rebel Jinwu General Ma Yue, into Tangut country and reached You Prefecture months later.

sentences.zh: 泚之僭逆，宦豎朱重曜頗親密用事，泚每呼之為兄。

translations.literal: In Zhu Ci's usurpation and rebellion, the eunuch Zhu Chongyao was quite intimate and wielded power; Zhu Ci always called him "elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: During his rebellion Zhu Ci relied heavily on the eunuch Zhu Chongyao, whom he affectionately addressed as "Brother."

sentences.zh: 時賊中以臘月大雨，偽星官謂泚曰：「當以宗中年長者禳其災變。」

translations.literal: At the time among the rebels there was heavy rain in the twelfth month; a false court astronomer told Zhu Ci: "One ought to use an elder of the clan to dispel this calamitous omen.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebel camp was lashed by unseasonable rains in the twelfth month. A sham court astronomer told Zhu Ci that the omen could be averted only by sacrificing the eldest member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 泚乃毒殺重曜，而以王禮葬焉。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci then poisoned and killed Chongyao, yet buried him with royal rites.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci poisoned Chongyao to death, then buried him with the honors due a prince.

sentences.zh: 及京師平，亦出其屍而斬之。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, they also exhumed his corpse and beheaded it.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was restored, Chongyao's body was dug up and decapitated as well.

sentences.zh: 姚令言自有傳。

translations.literal: Yao Lingyan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Lingyan is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 黃巢，曹州冤句人，本以販鹽為事。

translations.literal: Huang Chao, a native of Yuanqu in Cao Prefecture, originally made his living by selling salt.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao came from Yuanqu in Cao Prefecture and had begun as a salt smuggler.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，仍歲凶荒，人饑為盜，河南尤甚。

translations.literal: During the Qianfu era, year after year there was famine and disaster; hungry people became bandits, especially in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qianfu reign famine followed famine, and hunger drove men to banditry—nowhere more fiercely than in Henan.

sentences.zh: 初，里人王仙芝、尚君長聚盜，起于濮陽，攻剽城邑，陷曹、濮及鄆州。

translations.literal: At first, fellow townsmen Wang Xianzhi and Shang Junchang gathered bandits, rose at Puyang, attacked and plundered cities, and captured Cao, Pu, and Yan Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: It began when Wang Xianzhi and Shang Junchang, men of the same district, raised a band of outlaws at Puyang, raided towns and cities, and seized Cao, Pu, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 先有謠言云：「金色蛤蟆爭努眼，翻卻曹州天下反。」

translations.literal: There had earlier been a rumor saying: "Golden toads straining their eyes—overturn Cao Prefecture and all under heaven will rebel.
translations.idiomatic: A prophecy had already circulated: "Golden toads bulging their eyes—topple Cao Prefecture and the realm will rise in revolt.

sentences.zh: 及仙芝盜起，時議畏之。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi's banditry arose, contemporary opinion feared it.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzhi's uprising broke out, public alarm was immediate.

sentences.zh: 左金吾衛上將軍齊克讓為兗州節度使，以本軍討仙芝。

translations.literal: Senior General of the Left Jinwu Guard Qi Kerang became military governor of Yan Prefecture and led his own army to suppress Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Kerang, senior general of the Left Jinwu Guard, was appointed military governor of Yan Prefecture and marched against Xianzhi with his own troops.

sentences.zh: 仙芝懼，引眾曆陳、許、襄、鄧，無少長皆虜之，眾號三十萬。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was afraid, led his followers through Chen, Xu, Xiang, and Deng, capturing everyone young and old; his force was claimed to number three hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing defeat, Xianzhi swept through Chen, Xu, Xiang, and Deng, seizing every soul he could find, young or old, until his host was said to reach three hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，陷江陵。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, they captured Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the third year they took Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十月，又遣將徐君莒陷洪州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, he again sent the general Xu Junju to capture Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sent Xu Junju to seize Hong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時仙芝表請符節，不允。

translations.literal: At the time Xianzhi memorialized requesting official seals and credentials; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi then petitioned the throne for an official commission and military seal. The court refused.

sentences.zh: 以神策統軍使宋威為荊南節度招討使，中使楊復光為監軍。

translations.literal: Song Wei, commanding general of the Shence Army, was made Jingnan military governor and campaign commander; the palace envoy Yang Fuguang was made army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei, commander of the Shence Army, was named Jingnan military governor and chief pacification commissioner, with the eunuch Yang Fuguang as army monitor.

sentences.zh: 復光遣判官吳彥宏諭以朝廷釋罪，別加官爵，仙芝乃令尚君長、蔡溫球、楚彥威相次詣闕請罪，且求恩命。

translations.literal: Fuguang sent aide Wu Yanhong to tell them the court would pardon their crimes and additionally bestow titles and ranks; Xianzhi then ordered Shang Junchang, Cai Wenqiu, and Chu Yanwei in succession to go to court to plead guilty and also request gracious appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguang sent his aide Wu Yanhong to offer amnesty and promotion if they submitted. Xianzhi dispatched Shang Junchang, Cai Wenqiu, and Chu Yanwei in turn to the capital to confess their crimes and sue for favor.

sentences.zh: 時宋威害復光之功，並擒送闕，敕於狗脊嶺斬之。

translations.literal: At the time Song Wei, jealous of Fuguang's merit, captured them all and sent them to court; an edict ordered their execution at Gouji Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Song Wei, eager to steal Fuguang's credit, seized the envoys and sent them to the capital. An imperial order had them executed at Gouji Ridge.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，悉精銳擊官軍，威軍大敗，復光收其餘眾以統之。

translations.literal: The rebels were enraged and with all their elite forces attacked the imperial army; Wei's army was greatly defeated, and Fuguang gathered the remaining troops to command them.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the rebels threw their best troops against the government forces, shattered Wei's army, and Fuguang was left to gather the survivors under his own command.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以王鐸代為招討。

translations.literal: The court replaced him with Wang Duo as campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: The court replaced Wei with Wang Duo as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年八月，收復亳州，斬仙芝首獻于闕下。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fifth year, they recovered Bozhou and beheaded Xianzhi, presenting his head at the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fifth year the government retook Bozhou, struck off Xianzhi's head, and sent it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 先是，君長弟讓以兄奉使見誅，率部眾入嵖岈山。

translations.literal: Earlier, Junchang's younger brother Rang, because his elder brother had been executed while on a mission, led his band into the Chaya Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Junchang's younger brother Shang Rang saw his brother executed on a peace mission, he withdrew with his followers into the Chaya Mountains.

sentences.zh: 黃巢、黃揆昆仲八人，率盜數千依讓。

translations.literal: Huang Chao, Huang Kui, and seven other brothers—eight in all—led several thousand bandits to join Rang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao, Huang Kui, and six other brothers—eight Huang brothers in all—brought several thousand outlaws to Rang's banner.

sentences.zh: 月餘，眾至數萬。

translations.literal: After a little more than a month, their force grew to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Within little more than a month their numbers swelled to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 陷汝州，虜刺史王鐐，又掠關東。

translations.literal: They captured Ruzhou, took Governor Wang Liao prisoner, and also raided east of the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed Ruzhou, captured its prefect Wang Liao, and swept through the lands east of the Hangu Pass.

sentences.zh: 官軍加討，屢為所敗，其眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: The imperial army intensified the campaign but was repeatedly defeated by them; their force grew to over one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops pressed the pursuit but suffered defeat after defeat, while the rebel host passed one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 尚讓乃與群盜推巢為王，號沖天大將軍，仍署官屬，籓鎮不能制。

translations.literal: Shang Rang then together with the bandit chiefs raised Chao as king, with the title "Great General Who Charges Heaven," also appointing officials; the regional commands could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang and the other chieftains then proclaimed Huang Chao their king under the title Grand General Who Storms Heaven, set up a full roster of offices, and left the regional governors powerless to stop them.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平日久，人不知兵。

translations.literal: At the time the empire had long been at peace and people did not know warfare.
translations.idiomatic: The empire had known peace so long that war itself had been forgotten.

sentences.zh: 僖宗以幼主臨朝，號令出於臣下。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong, a young ruler on the throne, had his orders issued by subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong was a boy on the throne, and real power lay with the ministers around him.

sentences.zh: 南衙北司，迭相矛盾，以至九流濁亂，時多朋黨，小人才勝，君子道消，賢豪忌憤，退之草澤。

translations.literal: The southern court offices and northern palace eunuchs alternately opposed each other, so that all ranks were turbid and chaotic; there were many factions; petty men outdid talented ones, the way of gentlemen declined, worthy heroes nursed resentment and indignation, and withdrew to the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: The civil officials of the outer court and the eunuchs of the inner palace feuded without end until every level of government ran foul. Faction ruled the day: small men rose, gentlemen fell silent, and the able and upright, bitter and despairing, withdrew to the countryside.

sentences.zh: 既一朝有變，天下離心。

translations.literal: Once there was a sudden change in one morning, the empire lost its heart.
translations.idiomatic: When crisis struck at last, the people's loyalty to the throne dissolved overnight.

sentences.zh: 巢之起也，人士從而附之。

translations.literal: When Chao rose, scholars and gentlemen followed and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: As Huang Chao's rebellion gathered force, educated men flocked to his cause.

sentences.zh: 或巢馳檄四方，章奏論列，皆指目朝政之弊，蓋士不逞者之辭也。

translations.literal: Sometimes Chao sent proclamations in all directions; memorials and petitions analyzing affairs all pointed to the abuses of court governance—these were largely the words of frustrated scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His proclamations and petitions, circulated far and wide, denounced every corruption of the present reign—language that drew heavily on the grievances of failed scholars and displaced gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 巢徒党既盛，與仙芝為形援。

translations.literal: Chao's followers having grown strong, they formed a mutual strategic support with Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's movement grew strong enough to coordinate with Xianzhi as a second front.

sentences.zh: 及仙芝敗，東攻亳州不下，乃襲破沂州據之。

translations.literal: When Xianzhi was defeated, Chao attacked Bozhou in the east but could not take it; he then suddenly attacked and broke Yizhou and occupied it.
translations.idiomatic: After Xianzhi's fall, Huang Chao marched east against Bozhou but failed to take it; he then swung around, seized Yizhou by surprise, and held it.

sentences.zh: 仙芝餘黨悉附焉。

translations.literal: All of Xianzhi's remaining followers attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Every remnant of Xianzhi's band rallied to Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 時王鐸雖銜招討之權，緩於攻取。

translations.literal: At the time, though Wang Duo held the authority of campaign commander, he was slow to attack and seize.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo held the title of pacification commissioner but moved too slowly to strike.

sentences.zh: 時高駢鎮淮南，表請招討賊，許之，議加都統。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Pian governed Huainan and memorialized requesting to campaign against the bandits; this was granted, and there was discussion of adding the title of supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian, military governor of Huainan, petitioned to lead the campaign against the rebels. The court agreed and debated granting him the rank of supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 巢乃渡淮，偽降於駢。

translations.literal: Chao then crossed the Huai and falsely surrendered to Pian.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao crossed the Huai River and offered Gao Pian a false surrender.

sentences.zh: 駢遣將張璘率兵受降於天長鎮。

translations.literal: Pian sent the general Zhang Lin to lead troops to accept the surrender at Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian sent Zhang Lin with an army to receive the surrender at Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 巢擒璘殺之，因虜其眾。

translations.literal: Chao captured Lin and killed him, and also seized his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao seized Zhang Lin, killed him, and absorbed his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 尋南陷湖、湘，遂據交、廣。

translations.literal: Soon he captured Hunan and the Xiang region to the south, and then occupied Jiaozhi and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: He then overran Hunan and the Xiang basin, and pushed on to seize the far south around Jiaozhi and Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 托越州觀察使崔璆奏乞天平軍節度，朝議不允。

translations.literal: Through Yuezhou observation commissioner Cui Qiu he memorialized begging for the Tianping Army command; court deliberation did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Working through Cui Qiu, commissioner of Yuezhou, he petitioned for appointment as military governor of the Tianping Army. The court refused.

sentences.zh: 又乞除官，時宰臣鄭畋與樞密使楊復恭奏，欲請授同正員將軍。

translations.literal: He again begged for appointment to office; at the time Grand Councilor Zheng Tian and Privy Councilor Yang Fugong memorialized, wishing to request granting him General of the Fourth Rank.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned again for office. Grand Councilor Zheng Tian and Privy Councilor Yang Fugong recommended making him a general of the fourth rank with full salary.

sentences.zh: 盧攜駁其議，請授率府率，如其不受，請以高駢討之。

translations.literal: Lu Xie rebutted this proposal, requesting to grant him Chief of the Imperial Guard Office; if he did not accept, then requesting that Gao Pian suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xie objected, proposing instead the hollow post of director of the imperial guard bureau—and if Huang Chao rejected that, dispatching Gao Pian to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 及巢見詔，大詬執政，又自表乞安南都護、廣州節度，亦不允。

translations.literal: When Chao saw the edict, he greatly cursed the rulers; he also himself memorialized begging for Protector-General of Annam and Guangzhou military governorship—again not granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao read the edict he cursed the ministers in fury and petitioned on his own for the posts of Protector-General of Annam and military governor of Guangzhou. The court again refused.

sentences.zh: 然巢以士眾烏合，欲據南海之地，永為窠穴，坐邀朝命。

translations.literal: However, Chao's soldiers and crowds were a motley gathering; he wished to hold the lands of the Southern Sea as a permanent nest, sitting and demanding court appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his army was a loose confederation of adventurers, and he hoped to carve out a permanent base in the southern seas while bargaining with the throne for recognition.

sentences.zh: 是歲自春及夏，其眾大疫，死者十三四。

translations.literal: That year from spring through summer, his troops suffered a great epidemic; those who died were three or four out of ten.
translations.idiomatic: That year, from spring into summer, plague swept his camp and killed three or four men in every ten.

sentences.zh: 眾勸請北歸，以圖大利。

translations.literal: The crowd urged him to return north to pursue a great advantage.
translations.idiomatic: His followers pressed him to march north again while fortune still favored them.

sentences.zh: 巢不得已，廣明元年，北逾五嶺，犯湖、湘、江、浙，進逼廣陵，高駢閉門自固，所過鎮戍，望風降賊。

translations.literal: Chao had no choice; in the first year of Guangming, he went north crossing the Five Ridges, invaded Hu, Xiang, Jiang, and Zhe, advanced pressing on Guangling; Gao Pian shut his gates and held firm; garrisons he passed surrendered to the bandits at the sight of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao had little choice. In the first year of the Guangming era he crossed the Five Ridges northward, ravaged Hunan, the Yangzi delta, and Zhejiang, and bore down on Guangling. Gao Pian barricaded himself and would not fight; every garrison along the route surrendered at the first sight of rebel banners.

sentences.zh: 九月，渡淮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he crossed the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he crossed the Huai River.

sentences.zh: 十一月十七日，陷洛陽，留守劉允章率分司官迎之。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth day of the eleventh month, he captured Luoyang; the acting governor Liu Yunzhang led the branch-court officials to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth of the eleventh month he entered Luoyang, where the acting prefect Liu Yunzhang and the secondary capital officials went out to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 繼攻陝、虢，逼潼關，陷華州，留將奮鈐守之。

translations.literal: He then attacked Shan and Guo, pressed on Tong Pass, captured Hua Prefecture, and left the general Fen Qian to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: He pushed on against Shan and Guo, threatened Tong Pass, took Hua Prefecture, and left Fen Qian to hold it.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使李都詐進表於賊。

translations.literal: Hezhong military governor Li Du feigned submitting a memorial to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Li Du, military governor of Hezhong, sent in a memorial that only pretended loyalty while secretly siding with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以田令孜率神策、博野等軍十萬守潼關。

translations.literal: The court had Tian Lingzi lead one hundred thousand troops of the Shence, Boye, and other armies to guard Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: The court put Tian Lingzi at the head of one hundred thousand men from the Shence, Boye, and other armies to defend Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 時禁軍皆長安富族，世籍兩軍，豐給厚賜，高車大馬，以事權豪，自少迄長，不知戰陣。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial guard units were all wealthy families of Chang'an, registered for generations in the two armies, richly supplied with generous rewards, high carriages and big horses, serving the powerful and noble—they knew nothing of battle from youth to adulthood.
translations.idiomatic: The palace armies were drawn from Chang'an's rich families, hereditary members of the two guard corps, lavishly paid and richly equipped with fine carriages and tall horses as they waited on the great houses—they had never seen battle from boyhood to manhood.

sentences.zh: 初聞科集，父子聚哭，憚於出征。

translations.literal: When they first heard of the levy and assembly, fathers and sons gathered and wept, dreading going on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: When the draft was announced, fathers and sons wept together, terrified of marching to war.

sentences.zh: 各于兩市出值萬計，傭雇負販屠沽及病坊窮人，以為戰士，操刀載戟，不知钅敫銳。

translations.literal: Each paid out sums of ten thousand at the two markets, hiring porters, peddlers, butchers, wine-sellers, and poor men from charity wards as soldiers—they carried knives and bore halberds but did not know sharp from dull.
translations.idiomatic: Families spent fortunes in the markets to hire porters, peddlers, butchers, tavern hands, and beggars from the charity halls to stand in their place—men who could grip a blade or carry a halberd but could not tell a sharp edge from a blunt one.

sentences.zh: 復任宦官為將帥，驅以守關。

translations.literal: Eunuchs were again appointed as generals and commanders, driving them to guard the pass.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuch officers were put in command again and driven forward to hold the pass.

sentences.zh: 關之左有谷，可通行人，平時捉稅，禁人出入，謂之禁穀。

translations.literal: To the left of the pass there was a valley through which people could pass; ordinarily tolls were collected and passage forbidden—it was called Forbidden Valley.
translations.idiomatic: To the left of the pass lay a trail through a gorge where travelers were normally taxed and barred from crossing. It was known as Forbidden Gorge.

sentences.zh: 及賊至，官軍但守潼關，不防禁谷，以為穀既官禁，賊無得而逾也。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived, the imperial army only guarded Tong Pass and did not defend Forbidden Valley, thinking that since the valley was forbidden by the government, the rebels could not cross over it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came up, the government army held Tong Pass alone and left Forbidden Gorge unguarded, assuming that because the route was officially closed the enemy could never use it.

sentences.zh: 尚讓、林言率前鋒由禁谷而入，夾攻潼關。

translations.literal: Shang Rang and Lin Yan led the vanguard through Forbidden Valley and attacked Tong Pass from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Shang Rang and Lin Yan led the advance guard through Forbidden Gorge and struck the pass from front and rear.

sentences.zh: 官軍大潰，博野都徑還京師，燔掠西市。

translations.literal: The imperial army was utterly routed; the Boye contingent went straight back to the capital and burned and plundered the western market.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial line collapsed. The Boye troops turned straight for the capital and looted and burned the western market district.

sentences.zh: 十二月三日，僖宗夜自開遠門出，趨駱谷，諸王官屬相次奔命。

translations.literal: On the third day of the twelfth month, Emperor Xizong at night exited through Kaiyuan Gate and hurried toward Luogu; princes and officials followed one after another in flight.
translations.idiomatic: On the third of the twelfth month Emperor Xizong slipped out by night through Kaiyuan Gate and fled toward Luogu Pass, with princes and officials streaming after him in panic.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容使田令孜、王若儔收合禁軍扈從。

translations.literal: Army Observation Commissioners Tian Lingzi and Wang Ruochou gathered the imperial guard to escort him.
translations.idiomatic: The army commissioners Tian Lingzi and Wang Ruochou rallied the palace guard to escort the flight.

sentences.zh: 四日，賊至昭應，金吾大將軍張直方率在京兩班迎賊灞上。

translations.literal: On the fourth day, the rebels reached Zhaoying; Censor-in-Chief of the Jinwu Guard Zhang Zhifang led the two ranks of officials in the capital to welcome the rebels at Bashang.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourth the rebels reached Zhaoying. Zhang Zhifang, chief of the Jinwu Guard, led the full corps of capital officials out to Bashang to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 五日，賊陷京師。

translations.literal: On the fifth day, the rebels captured the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth the rebels took Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 時巢眾累年為盜，行伍不勝其富，遇窮民于路，爭行施遺。

translations.literal: At the time Chao's followers had been bandits for many years; the ranks could not bear their wealth—when they met poor people on the road, they all competed to give them things.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's men had grown rich from years of plunder, and their ranks overflowed with loot. On the road they vied with one another to press gifts on every poor passerby they met.

sentences.zh: 既入春明門，坊市聚觀，尚讓慰曉市人曰：「黃王為生靈，不似李家不恤汝輩，但各安家。」

translations.literal: After entering Chunming Gate, the wards and markets gathered to watch; Shang Rang comforted and explained to the townspeople: "King Huang acts for the people—unlike the Li family who did not care for you. Simply settle peacefully in your homes.
translations.idiomatic: Once they passed Chunming Gate, crowds lined the streets to watch. Shang Rang called out reassurance to the townspeople: "King Huang comes for the people's sake, not like the House of Li, who never cared for you. Go home and live in peace.

sentences.zh: 巢賊眾競投物遺人。

translations.literal: Chao's bandits competed to throw goods and give things to people.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's soldiers showered the crowd with gifts.

sentences.zh: 十三日，賊巢僭位，國號大齊，年稱金統，仍御樓宣赦，且陳符命曰：「唐帝知朕起義，改元廣明，以文字言之，唐已無天分矣。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day, the bandit Chao usurped the throne; the state name was Great Qi, the era name Jintong; he also ascended the tower to proclaim amnesty, and stated the mandate of signs: "The Tang emperor knew I rose in righteous uprising and changed the era to Guangming—speaking in terms of characters, Tang no longer has Heaven's portion.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth Huang Chao declared himself emperor. His dynasty was called Great Qi, his reign era Golden Rule. From the palace tower he proclaimed a general amnesty and announced heaven's verdict: "The Tang emperor knew of my righteous uprising when he changed the era to Guangming. Read the characters rightly, and Tang has lost the Mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 『唐』去『醜』、『口』而安『黃』，天意令黃在唐下，乃黃家日月也。

translations.literal: Remove "chou" and "kou" from "Tang" and place "Huang" in peace—Heaven's intent places Huang beneath Tang's structure, thus it is the sun and moon of the Huang house.
translations.idiomatic: Strip away the components for "ugly" and "mouth" from the character for Tang, and "yellow" stands whole beneath it—heaven means the Huang clan to inherit the sun and moon of empire.

sentences.zh: 土德生金，予以金王，宜改年為金統。」

translations.literal: Earth virtue generates metal; I take metal as king—it is fitting to change the era to Jintong.
translations.idiomatic: Earth begets metal; I reign by the power of metal. The era should therefore be called Golden Rule.

sentences.zh: 賊搜訪舊宰相不獲，以前浙東觀察使崔璆、楊希古、尚讓、趙章為四相，孟楷、蓋洪為左右軍中尉，費傳古為樞密使，王璠為京兆尹，許建、朱實、劉塘為軍庫使，朱溫、張言、彭攢、季逵為諸衛大將軍、四面游奕使。

translations.literal: The rebels searched for former chancellors but did not find them; they appointed former Zhedong observation commissioner Cui Qiu, Yang Xigu, Shang Rang, and Zhao Zhang as the four chancellors; Meng Kai and Gai Hong as left and right army commissioners; Fei Chuangu as privy councilor; Wang Fan as metropolitan governor of Jingzhao; Xu Jian, Zhu Shi, and Liu Tang as military warehouse commissioners; Zhu Wen, Zhang Yan, Peng Zan, and Ji Kui as grand generals of the various guards and mobile patrol commissioners on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to find former chief ministers, the rebels named Cui Qiu, once commissioner of Zhedong, together with Yang Xigu, Shang Rang, and Zhao Zhang as the four chancellors. Meng Kai and Gai Hong became left and right army commissioners; Fei Chuangu, privy councilor; Wang Fan, metropolitan governor of Jingzhao; Xu Jian, Zhu Shi, and Liu Tang, directors of the military stores; and Zhu Wen, Zhang Yan, Peng Zan, and Ji Kui grand generals of the guard corps and commissioners of mobile patrols on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 又選驍勇形體魁梧者五百人，曰功臣。

translations.literal: They also selected five hundred men who were valiant and of imposing physique, calling them "meritorious officials."
translations.idiomatic: They further chose five hundred of the fiercest and tallest warriors and styled them the Meritorious Guard.

sentences.zh: 令其甥林言為軍使，比之控鶴。

translations.literal: They made his nephew Lin Yan army commissioner, comparing them to the Crane Controllers.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao appointed his nephew Lin Yan to command them, on the model of the Tang dynasty's Crane Controlling Guard.

sentences.zh: 中和元年二月，尚讓寇鳳翔，鄭畋出師禦之，大敗賊于龍尾坡，畋乃馳檄告喻天下籓鎮。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Zhonghe, Shang Rang raided Fengxiang; Zheng Tian marched out his army to resist him and greatly defeated the rebels at Longwei Slope; Tian then sent urgent proclamations to inform and admonish all the frontier military governors under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Zhonghe (881), Shang Rang raided Fengxiang. Zheng Tian took the field against him and routed the rebel army at Longwei Slope, then dispatched urgent proclamations calling upon the empire's regional commanders to rise in the dynasty's defense.

sentences.zh: 四月，涇原行軍唐弘夫之師屯渭北，河中王重榮之師屯沙苑，易定王處存之師屯渭橋，鄜延拓拔思恭之師屯武功，鳳翔鄭畋之師屯盩至。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the army of Tang Hongfu, acting commander of Jingyuan, encamped north of the Wei; the army of Wang Chongrong of Hezhong encamped at Shayuan; the army of Wang Chucun of Yiding encamped at Weiqiao; the army of Tuoba Sigong of Yan-Yan encamped at Wugong; the army of Zheng Tian of Fengxiang encamped at Zhouzhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, Tang Hongfu's Jingyuan expeditionary force camped north of the Wei River; Wang Chongrong's Hezhong army at Shayuan; Wang Chucun's Yiding army at Weiqiao; Tuoba Sigong's Yan-Yan army at Wugong; and Zheng Tian's Fengxiang army at Zhouzhi.

sentences.zh: 六月，邠寧朱玫之師屯興平，忠武之師三千屯武功。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the army of Zhu Mei of Binning encamped at Xingping, and three thousand troops of Zhongwu encamped at Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Zhu Mei's Binning force took position at Xingping, while three thousand Zhongwu troops encamped at Wugong.

sentences.zh: 是歲諸侯勤王之師，四面俱會。

translations.literal: In that year the armies of the feudal lords who came to rescue the Son of Heaven converged from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: That year the relief armies of the regional lords converged upon the capital from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 十二月，宰相王鐸率荊、襄之師自行在至，鄭畋帳下小校竇玫者，驍勇無敵，每夜率敢死之士百人，直入京師，放火燔諸門，斬級而還，賊人悚駭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Chancellor Wang Duo led the armies of Jing and Xiang from the temporary imperial residence; Dou Mei, a junior officer under Zheng Tian's command, was matchlessly fierce and brave—each night he led a hundred dare-to-die men straight into the capital, set fires and burned the gates, cut off heads and returned, and the rebels were struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Chancellor Wang Duo arrived from the court's temporary seat at Xiang with the armies of Jing and Xiang. Among Zheng Tian's officers was the junior commander Dou Mei, a warrior without peer: every night he led a hundred volunteers deep into the capital, torched the gate towers, beheaded the enemy, and withdrew before dawn, leaving the rebels shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 時京畿百姓皆砦于山谷，累年廢耕耘，賊坐空城，賦輸無入，穀食騰踴，米斗三十千。

translations.literal: At that time the common people of the capital region all fortified themselves in mountain valleys; for years they abandoned plowing and sowing; the rebels sat in an empty city; tax and grain deliveries had no intake; grain food surged in price—a peck of rice cost thirty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: By then the people of the capital districts had fled into the hills and built stockades; fields lay untilled for years. The rebels held an empty city with no revenue coming in, and grain prices soared until a single peck of rice sold for thirty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 官軍皆執山砦百姓，鬻于賊為食，人獲數十萬。

translations.literal: The government armies all seized the common people in the mountain stockades and sold them to the rebels for food; people captured numbered in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops rounded up civilians from the mountain refuges and sold them to the rebels for provisions; the number of people thus taken reached into the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 朝士皆往來同、華，或以賣餅為業，因奔於河中。

translations.literal: Court officials all traveled back and forth between Tong and Hua, some taking up the trade of selling cakes, and thereby fled to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials shuttled between Tongzhou and Huazhou, some earning their bread by selling flatcakes, until at last they escaped across to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 宰相崔沆、豆盧瓚扈從不及，匿之別墅，所由搜索嚴急，乃微行入永甯里張直方之家。

translations.literal: Chancellors Cui Hang and Doulu Zan could not keep up with the imperial entourage and hid in separate villas; the authorities searched with extreme severity, so they went in disguise into the home of Zhang Zhifang in Yongning Ward.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellors Cui Hang and Doulu Zan had fallen behind the imperial procession and concealed themselves in country villas. When the search grew relentless, they slipped through the streets in disguise and took shelter in the house of Zhang Zhifang in Yongning Ward.

sentences.zh: 朝貴怙直方之豪，多依之。

translations.literal: The court nobility relied on Zhifang's power and many depended on him.
translations.idiomatic: High officials at court leaned on Zhang Zhifang's wealth and influence, and many made their refuge under his roof.

sentences.zh: 既而或告賊云：「直方謀反，納亡命。」

translations.literal: Before long someone reported to the rebels, saying: "Zhifang plots rebellion and harbors fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: Before long someone informed the rebels: "Zhang Zhifang is plotting rebellion and sheltering outlaws.

sentences.zh: 賊攻其第，直方族誅，沆、瓚數百人皆遇害。

translations.literal: The rebels attacked his residence; Zhifang's entire clan was executed; Hang, Zan, and several hundred others all met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels stormed his mansion. Zhang Zhifang's entire clan was put to the sword, and Cui Hang, Doulu Zan, and several hundred others perished with them.

sentences.zh: 自是賊始酷虐，族滅居人。

translations.literal: From this time the rebels first turned cruel and tyrannical, exterminating whole clans of residents.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the rebels' rule turned savage; they began to wipe out entire households of the city's people.

sentences.zh: 遣使傳命召故相駙馬都尉于琮於其第。

translations.literal: They sent envoys bearing orders summoning the former chancellor and imperial son-in-law, Chief Commandant Yu Cong, to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: They dispatched messengers with orders summoning the former chancellor and imperial son-in-law, Yu Cong, Chief Commandant of the imperial guard, to appear at his own mansion.

sentences.zh: 琮曰：「吾唐室大臣，不可佐黃家草昧，加之老疾。」

translations.literal: Cong said: "I am a great minister of the Tang house; I cannot assist the Huang family's rude beginnings; moreover I am old and ill.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cong replied: "I am a minister of the Tang dynasty. I will not serve the Huang clan in their hour of raw ambition—and besides, I am old and infirm.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，令誅之。

translations.literal: The rebels were enraged and ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels flew into a rage and ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 廣德公主並賊號咷而謂曰：「予即天子女，不宜復存，可與相公俱死。」

translations.literal: Princess Guangde wailed bitterly and said to him: "I am the daughter of Heaven; it is not fitting that I should continue to live—I may die together with the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Guangde came forward wailing and cried out: "I am a daughter of the Son of Heaven. I cannot outlive this shame—let me die with my husband the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 是日並遇害。

translations.literal: On that day both met with disaster together.
