translations.idiomatic: That same day they were both killed.

sentences.zh: 二年，王處存合忠武之師，敗賊將尚讓，乘勝入京師，賊遁去。

translations.literal: In the second year, Wang Chucun combined with the army of Zhongwu, defeated the rebel general Shang Rang, and following victory entered the capital; the rebels fled away.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year (882), Wang Chucun joined forces with the Zhongwu army, defeated the rebel commander Shang Rang, and pressed the advantage into the capital. The rebels withdrew.

sentences.zh: 處存不為備，是夜復為賊寇襲，官軍不利。

translations.literal: Chucun made no preparations; that night he was again raided by rebel bandits, and the government army fared badly.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun failed to secure his gains. That very night the rebels counterattacked, and the imperial army suffered a sharp reverse.

sentences.zh: 賊怒坊市百姓迎王師，乃下令洗城，丈夫丁壯，殺戮殆盡，流血成渠。

translations.literal: The rebels, enraged that the people of the wards and markets had welcomed the royal army, then issued an order to "wash the city"—able-bodied men were slaughtered almost to the last, and blood ran in channels.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged that the townspeople had welcomed the imperial troops, the rebels ordered a massacre of the city. Every able-bodied man they could find was cut down until blood flowed in the streets like irrigation ditches.

sentences.zh: 九月，賊將同州刺史朱溫降重榮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the rebel general Zhu Wen, governor of Tongzhou, surrendered to Chongrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, the rebel commander Zhu Wen, military governor of Tongzhou, defected to Wang Chongrong.

sentences.zh: 十一月，李克用率代北之師，自夏陽渡河，屯沙苑。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Li Keyong led the army of northern Dai, crossed the river from Xiayang, and encamped at Shayuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Li Keyong led his army from the northern frontier, crossed the Yellow River at Xiayang, and encamped at Shayuan.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，敗黃揆于沙苑，進營乾坑。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, he defeated Huang Kui at Shayuan and advanced to camp at Gan Pit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year (883), he routed Huang Kui at Shayuan and pushed forward to encamp at Gan Pit.

sentences.zh: 二月，賊將林言、趙章、尚讓率眾十萬援華州。

translations.literal: In the second month, the rebel generals Lin Yan, Zhao Zhang, and Shang Rang led a host of one hundred thousand to relieve Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, the rebel generals Lin Yan, Zhao Zhang, and Shang Rang marched one hundred thousand men to relieve the siege of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 克用合河中、易定、忠武之師，戰于梁田坡，大敗賊軍，俘斬數萬，乘勝攻華州，塹柵以環之。

translations.literal: Keyong combined the armies of Hezhong, Yiding, and Zhongwu and fought at Liangtian Slope, greatly defeating the rebel army, capturing and slaying tens of thousands; following victory he attacked Huazhou and dug trenches and palisades to encircle it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong united the forces of Hezhong, Yiding, and Zhongwu and met the enemy at Liangtian Slope, where he shattered the rebel army and killed or captured tens of thousands. Pressing the attack on Huazhou, he ringed the city with trenches and stockades.

sentences.zh: 克用騎軍在渭北，令薛志勤、康君立每夜突入京師，燔積聚，俘級而旋。

translations.literal: Keyong's cavalry was north of the Wei; he ordered Xue Zhiqin and Kang Junli each night to burst into the capital, burn stored supplies, capture heads, and wheel about and return.
translations.idiomatic: With his cavalry north of the Wei, Li Keyong sent Xue Zhiqin and Kang Junli on nightly raids into the capital to burn grain stores, take heads, and withdraw before dawn.

sentences.zh: 黃揆棄華州，官軍收城。

translations.literal: Huang Kui abandoned Huazhou, and the government army recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kui abandoned Huazhou, and the imperial army reoccupied the city.

sentences.zh: 四月八日，克用合忠武騎將龐從遇賊于渭南，決戰三捷，大敗賊軍。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the fourth month, Keyong combined with the Zhongwu cavalry commander Pang Cong and encountered the rebels at Weinan; after three decisive battles he greatly defeated the rebel army.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the fourth month, Li Keyong joined the Zhongwu cavalry commander Pang Cong and met the rebels at Weinan. Three pitched battles brought a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 十日夜，賊巢散走。

translations.literal: On the night of the tenth, the band of Chao scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the tenth, Huang Chao's forces broke and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，克用由光泰門入，收京師。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day, Keyong entered through Guangtai Gate and recovered the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the following morning, Li Keyong entered the capital through Guangtai Gate and took possession of the city.

sentences.zh: 巢賊出藍田、七盤路，東走關東。

translations.literal: Chao's rebels went out by the Lantian and Qipan routes and fled east toward the eastern passes.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's remnant army escaped by the Lantian and Qipan roads and fled east into the lands beyond the passes.

sentences.zh: 天下兵馬都監押楊復光露布獻捷於行在，陳破賊事狀曰：

translations.literal: Yang Fuguang, overall military inspector and commissioner, presented a victory bulletin to the temporary imperial residence, setting forth the account of defeating the rebels, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fuguang, commissioner and overall military inspector, submitted a victory dispatch to the court in exile, reporting the defeat of the rebels in these terms:

sentences.zh: 頃者妖興霧市，盜嘯叢祠，而岳牧籓侯，備盜不謹。

translations.literal: Recently demons arose in the misty markets and robbers howled from clustered shrines, while the governors and frontier lords were not careful in guarding against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Of late, sorcery has stirred in the marketplaces and outlaws have roared from every roadside shrine, while the provincial governors and frontier lords failed to keep proper watch against brigandage.

sentences.zh: 謂大同之運，常可容奸；

translations.literal: They supposed that the fortune of Great Unity could always harbor treachery;
translations.idiomatic: They assumed that under the Mandate of Great Unity treachery could always find room;

sentences.zh: 謂無事之秋，縱其長惡。

translations.literal: they supposed that in a season of peace they might indulge its growing evil.
translations.idiomatic: they assumed that in untroubled times they could indulge wickedness and let it grow unchecked.

sentences.zh: 賊首黃巢，因得充盈窟穴，蔓延萑蒲，驅我蒸黎，徇其凶逆。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftain Huang Chao thereby filled his lair to overflowing, spread through the reeds and rushes, drove our common people, and enforced his fierce rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the rebel chieftain Huang Chao filled his dens to overflowing, spread like weeds through the marshes, drove our people before him, and pressed his violent revolt upon the realm.

sentences.zh: 展鉏鶴以成鋒刃，殺耕牛以恣燔砲，魑魅晝行，虺蜴夜噬。

translations.literal: He sharpened hoes and cranes into blades, slaughtered plow oxen to indulge in roasting siege engines; goblins walked by day and venomous serpents fed by night.
translations.idiomatic: He turned farming tools into weapons, butchered draft oxen to fuel his siege engines; demons walked abroad in daylight and poisonous serpents fed under cover of night.

sentences.zh: 自南海失守，湖外喪師，養虎災深，馴梟逆大，物無不害，惡靡不為，豺狼貽朝市之憂，瘡磐及腹心之痛。

translations.literal: From the loss of the southern sea frontier and the destruction of armies beyond the lakes, the calamity of nurturing a tiger grew deep and the perversity of taming an owl grew great; nothing escaped harm and no evil went undone; wolves and jackals brought worry to the court and marketplace, and sores spread to the pain of the heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the southern coast and the ruin of our armies in the lake districts, the disaster of raising a tiger deepened and the folly of domesticating an owl bore its bitter fruit. Nothing was spared, no cruelty left undone; wolves and jackals haunted the capital's markets, and the wound festered to the empire's very core.

sentences.zh: 遂至毒流萬姓，盜汙兩京。

translations.literal: It reached the point that poison flowed among the myriad people and robbers defiled the Two Capitals.
translations.idiomatic: At last poison ran through the lives of common people, and the bandits defiled both imperial capitals.

sentences.zh: 衣冠銜塗炭之悲，郡邑起丘墟之歎。

translations.literal: Officials and gentry bore the grief of dust and charcoal; commanderies and districts raised the sigh of mounds and ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials wore the grief of ashes and cinders; town after town echoed with the lament of rubble and empty streets.

sentences.zh: 萬方共怒，十道齊攻，伏九廟之威靈，殄積年之凶醜。

translations.literal: The myriad regions shared in anger; ten circuits attacked together; relying on the awesomeness of the Nine Temples, they exterminated the accumulated years' fierce villainy.
translations.idiomatic: All under heaven burned with a common wrath; ten circuits struck as one, invoking the majesty of the imperial ancestors to destroy a villainy years in the making.

sentences.zh: 河中節度使王重榮神資壯烈，天付機謀，誓立功名，志安家國。

translations.literal: Wang Chongrong, military governor of Hezhong, possessed a divine endowment of bold fierceness; Heaven entrusted him with stratagem; he vowed to establish merit and was resolved to settle the state and homeland.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongrong, military governor of Hezhong, was endowed with heroic courage and Heaven-given cunning. He swore to win glory in battle and set his heart on restoring the realm.

sentences.zh: 至於屯田待敵，率士當沖，收百姓十萬餘家，降賊党三萬餘眾。

translations.literal: As to encamping in the fields awaiting the enemy and leading soldiers to meet the shock, he received more than one hundred thousand households of common people and caused more than thirty thousand rebel partisans to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He held his ground in the open country, met the enemy head-on, sheltered more than one hundred thousand civilian households, and accepted the surrender of over thirty thousand rebel followers.

sentences.zh: 法當持重，功遂晚成，久稽原野之刑，未快雷霆之怒。

translations.literal: By law he ought to have been deliberate, and so his achievement was slow in completion; long he delayed the punishment on the open plain, and the thunderbolt's wrath was not yet satisfied.
translations.idiomatic: Strategy demanded patience, and so his triumph came late; too long the reckoning on the battlefield was deferred, and Heaven's wrath had not yet been fully spent.

sentences.zh: 自收同、華，逼近京師，夕烽高照于國門，遊騎俯臨於灞岸。

translations.literal: Since recovering Tong and Hua and pressing close to the capital, evening beacon fires shone high at the national gate and roaming cavalry looked down upon the Ba shore.
translations.idiomatic: Once Tongzhou and Huazhou were recovered and the army drew near the capital, signal fires blazed each evening at the city gates and scouting horsemen ranged the banks of the Ba River.

sentences.zh: 既知四隅斷絕，百計奔沖，如窮鳥觸籠，似飛蛾赴燭。

translations.literal: When they knew that all four corners were cut off, they exhausted every stratagem in desperate flight, like a trapped bird striking its cage or a flying moth rushing into the flame.
translations.idiomatic: Finding every escape closed, the rebels tried every desperate stratagem, like birds beating against a cage or moths hurling themselves into flame.

sentences.zh: 雁門節度使李克用神傳將略，天付忠貞，機謀與武藝皆優，臣節共本心相稱。

translations.literal: Li Keyong, military governor of Yanmen, inherited divine transmission of generalship; Heaven entrusted him with loyalty and steadfastness; stratagem and martial skill were both superior, and ministerial integrity matched his inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong, military governor of Yanmen, was born to the art of command and entrusted by Heaven with unwavering loyalty. His cunning and his sword arm were alike unmatched, and his devotion to the throne was the equal of his courage.

sentences.zh: 殺賊無非手刃，入陣率以身先，可謂雄才，得名飛將。

translations.literal: In slaying rebels none were not killed by his own hand; entering battle he always led from the front—he may be called a heroic talent and deserved the name Flying General.
translations.idiomatic: He killed rebels with his own blade and always led the charge himself—a true hero, worthy of the title Flying General.

sentences.zh: 自統本軍南下，與臣同力前驅，雖在寢餐，不忘寇孽。

translations.literal: Since commanding his own army southward, he joined his strength with mine as vanguard; even at meals and rest he did not forget the bandit scourge.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he marched south at the head of his own army, he fought alongside me in the vanguard; even at meals and in sleep he never forgot the enemy.

sentences.zh: 今月八日，遣衙隊前鋒楊守宗、河中騎將白志遷、橫野軍使滿存、躡雲都將丁行存、朝邑鎮將康師貞、忠武黃頭軍使龐從等三十都，隨李克用自光泰門先入京師，力摧凶寇。

translations.literal: On the eighth of this month, I dispatched the vanguard of the yamen guard Yang Shouzong, the Hezhong cavalry commander Bai Zhixian, the Hengye army commissioner Man Cun, the Nieyun commander Ding Xingcun, the Chaoyi garrison commander Kang Shizhen, the Zhongwu Yellow Head army commissioner Pang Cong, and thirty commands altogether, who followed Li Keyong through Guangtai Gate to enter the capital first and forcefully crushed the fierce rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth of this month I sent forward thirty commands under Yang Shouzong of the yamen guard, Bai Zhixian of the Hezhong cavalry, Man Cun of the Hengye army, Ding Xingcun of the Nieyun command, Kang Shizhen of Chaoyi, Pang Cong of the Zhongwu Yellow Head army, and others. Following Li Keyong through Guangtai Gate, they were first into the capital and broke the rebel line.

sentences.zh: 又遣河中將劉讓、王環、冀君武、孫珙，忠武將喬從遇，鄭滑將韓從威，荊南將申屠悰，滄州將賈滔，易定將張仲慶，壽州將張行方，天德將顧彥朗，左神策弩手甄君楚、公孫佐，橫沖軍使楊守亮，躡雲都將高周彝，忠順都將胡真，絳州監軍毛宣伯、聶弘裕等七十都繼進。

translations.literal: I also dispatched the Hezhong generals Liu Rang, Wang Huan, Ji Junwu, and Sun Gong; the Zhongwu general Qiao Congyu; the Zheng-Hua general Han Congwei; the Jingnan general Shentu Cong; the Cangzhou general Jia Tao; the Yiding general Zhang Zhongqing; the Shouzhou general Zhang Xingfang; the Tiande general Gu Yanlang; the Left Divine Stratagem crossbowmen Zhen Junchu and Gongsun Zuo; the Hengchong army commissioner Yang Shouliang; the Nieyun commander Gao Zhouyi; the Zhongshun commander Hu Zhen; the Jiangzhou military commissioners Mao Xuanbo and Nie Hongyu, and seventy commands in succession to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy more commands followed in succession: the Hezhong generals Liu Rang, Wang Huan, Ji Junwu, and Sun Gong; Qiao Congyu of Zhongwu; Han Congwei of Zheng-Hua; Shentu Cong of Jingnan; Jia Tao of Cangzhou; Zhang Zhongqing of Yiding; Zhang Xingfang of Shouzhou; Gu Yanlang of Tiande; the Left Divine Stratagem crossbowmen Zhen Junchu and Gongsun Zuo; Yang Shouliang of the Hengchong army; Gao Zhouyi of the Nieyun command; Hu Zhen of Zhongshun; and the Jiangzhou commissioners Mao Xuanbo and Nie Hongyu.

sentences.zh: 賊尚為堅陣，來抗官軍。

translations.literal: The rebels still held a firm formation and came to resist the government army.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels still held their ground in tight formation and came out to meet the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 雁門李克用率勵驍雄，整齊金革，叫噪而聲將動瓦，喑嗚而氣欲吞沙，寬列戈矛，密張羅網。

translations.literal: Li Keyong of Yanmen roused the fierce and heroic, put arms and armor in good order; their shouts and clamor nearly shook the roof tiles, their battle cries seemed to swallow the sands; he spread lances and halberds in broad array and drew the net tight.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong of Yanmen roused his fiercest warriors and dressed the ranks in gleaming armor. Their battle cries shook the rooftops; their war chants seemed to swallow the desert wind. Spears and halberds spread wide; the net of encirclement drew tight.

sentences.zh: 於是麾軍背擊，分騎橫沖，日明而劍躍飛輪，風急而旗開走電。

translations.literal: Thereupon he commanded the army to strike from behind and divided the cavalry to charge crosswise; as the sun brightened swords leapt like flying wheels, and as the wind rose banners opened like running lightning.
translations.idiomatic: Then he wheeled his army to strike from the rear and sent cavalry to charge from the flanks. In the brightening sun swords flashed like spinning wheels; in the rising wind banners unfurled like lightning across the field.

sentences.zh: 使賊如浪，便可塞流；

translations.literal: Had the rebels been like waves, they could have been dammed and stopped;
translations.idiomatic: Had the enemy been a flood, it would have been dammed and turned back;

sentences.zh: 使賊如山，亦須折角。

translations.literal: had the rebels been like mountains, their corners would still have had to be broken.
translations.idiomatic: had they been a mountain, its ridges would still have been shattered.

sentences.zh: 蹂踐則橫屍入地，騰淩則積血成塵，不煩即墨之牛，若駕昆陽之象。

translations.literal: Where they trampled, corpses lay crosswise in the earth; where they leapt over, accumulated blood became dust—without need of the cattle of Jimo, as if driving the elephant legions of Kunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Where the charge passed, bodies piled upon the ground; where the horses leapt, blood turned the dust to mud—as though the oxen of Jimo and the elephant hosts of Kunyang had ridden to war together.

sentences.zh: 楊守宗等齊驅直入，合勢夾攻，從卯至申，群凶大潰。

translations.literal: Yang Shouzong and the others drove together straight in; combining their momentum they attacked from both sides; from the hour mao to the hour shen the mass of villains utterly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouzong and the rest drove straight into the enemy line, converging from both flanks. From dawn until mid-afternoon the rebel host broke completely.

sentences.zh: 自望春宮前蹙殺，至昇陽殿下攻圍，戈不濫揮，矢無虛發。

translations.literal: From the killing press before Wangchun Palace to the siege and encirclement below Shengyang Hall, spears were not swung at random and arrows found no empty mark.
translations.idiomatic: From the slaughter before Wangchun Palace to the encirclement below Shengyang Hall, every spear stroke fell true and every arrow found its mark.

sentences.zh: 其賊一時奔走，南入商山，徒延漏刃之生，佇作飲頭之器。

translations.literal: The rebels at one stroke fled in flight, entering south into the Shang Mountains—merely prolonging a life beneath the spared blade, waiting to become vessels for drinking heads.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke and ran south into the Shang Mountains, buying only a few hours beneath the sword, destined soon to furnish drinking cups from their skulls.

sentences.zh: 自收平京闕，二面皆立大功，若破敵摧凶，李克用實居其首。

translations.literal: Since recovering and pacifying the capital, on two fronts great achievements were established; in breaking the enemy and crushing the villainous, Li Keyong truly stood first.
translations.idiomatic: In the recovery and pacification of the capital, great deeds were done on every front; but in breaking the enemy and crushing the rebels, Li Keyong stood first among them all.

sentences.zh: 其餘將佐，同效驅馳。

translations.literal: The remaining generals and aides alike exerted themselves in the charge.
translations.idiomatic: The other commanders and their officers fought with equal zeal.

sentences.zh: 兼臣所部領萬餘人，數歲櫛風沐雨。

translations.literal: Together with more than ten thousand men under my own command, for several years we endured wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the ten thousand men under my own command, we had endured years of wind and rain in the field.

sentences.zh: 既茲平蕩，並錄以聞。

translations.literal: Now that the pacification is complete, all are recorded and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Now that order is restored, I report these deeds for the record.

sentences.zh: 五月，巢賊先鋒將孟楷攻蔡州，節度使秦宗權以兵逆戰，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the vanguard rebel general Meng Kai attacked Caizhou; the military governor Qin Zongquan met him with troops in counter-battle and was defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Huang Chao's vanguard commander Meng Kai attacked Caizhou. The military governor Qin Zongquan marched out to meet him and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 攻城急，宗權乃稱臣於賊。

translations.literal: The siege grew urgent; Zongquan then declared himself a subject of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege tightened, Qin Zongquan submitted and declared himself a vassal of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 遂攻陳、許，營于溵水。

translations.literal: He then attacked Chen and Xu and encamped at the Yin River.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned against Chen and Xu and encamped on the banks of the Yin River.

sentences.zh: 陳州刺史趙犨迎戰，敗賊前鋒，生擒孟楷，斬之。

translations.literal: The prefect of Chenzhou, Zhao Chao, met them in battle, defeated the rebel vanguard, captured Meng Kai alive, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chao, prefect of Chenzhou, gave battle, routed the rebel vanguard, captured Meng Kai alive, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 黃巢素寵楷，悲惜之。

translations.literal: Huang Chao had always favored Kai and grieved over the loss.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao had long favored Meng Kai and mourned his death deeply.

sentences.zh: 乃悉眾攻陳州，營於城北五里，為宮闕之制，曰八仙營。

translations.literal: He then mustered his entire host to attack Chenzhou, encamped five li north of the city wall, and built in the style of palace halls—a camp called the Eight Immortals Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered his full strength against Chenzhou, pitching camp five li north of the walls in a compound built like an imperial palace—a fortress they called the Eight Immortals Camp.

sentences.zh: 於是自唐、鄧、許、汝、孟、洛、鄭、汴、曹、濮、徐、兗數十州，畢罹其毒。

translations.literal: From this, among several tens of prefectures including Tang, Deng, Xu, Ru, Meng, Luo, Zheng, Bian, Cao, Pu, Xu, and Yan, all alike suffered their poison.
translations.idiomatic: From that point dozens of prefectures—Tang, Deng, Xu, Ru, Meng, Luo, Zheng, Bian, Cao, Pu, Xu, and Yan among them—alike fell victim to their ravages.

sentences.zh: 賊圍陳郡百日，關東仍歲無耕稼，人餓倚牆壁間，賊俘人而食，日殺數千。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged Chen Commandery for one hundred days; in the eastern passes for successive years there was no plowing or harvest; people starved leaning against walls; the rebels captured people to eat and killed several thousand each day.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels besieged Chenzhou for a hundred days. East of the passes fields went unplanted year after year; the starving collapsed against city walls. The rebels took captives for food and slaughtered several thousand people each day.

sentences.zh: 賊有舂磨砦，為巨碓數百，生納人於臼碎之，合骨而食，其流毒若是。

translations.literal: The rebels had pounding-grinding stockades with several hundred great pestles; they put living people into the mortars and crushed them, eating them bones and all—their flowing poison was like this.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels maintained "grinding camps" fitted with hundreds of giant mortars into which living captives were thrown and pulverized, then consumed bones and all. Such was the depth of their cruelty.

sentences.zh: 趙犨求援於太原。

translations.literal: Zhao Chao sought aid from Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chao sent to Taiyuan for relief.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，李克用率山西諸軍，由蒲、陝濟河，會關東諸侯，赴援陳州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, Li Keyong led the armies of Shanxi, crossed the river by Pu and Shan, joined the feudal lords of the eastern passes, and marched to relieve Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year (884), Li Keyong led the armies of Shanxi, crossed the Yellow River from Pu and Shan, joined the lords of the eastern passes, and marched to the relief of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，諸侯之師復集。

translations.literal: In the third month, the armies of the feudal lords assembled again.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the allied armies gathered once more.

sentences.zh: 四月，官軍敗賊于太康，俘斬萬計，拔其四壁。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, the government army defeated the rebels at Taikang, capturing and slaying enemies by the tens of thousands, and captured their four walled camps.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the imperial army routed the rebels at Taikang, killing and capturing them by the tens of thousands and taking all four of their fortified camps.

sentences.zh: 又敗賊將黃鄴于西華，拔其壁。

translations.literal: They again defeated the rebel general Huang Ye at Xihua and captured his camp.
translations.idiomatic: They defeated the rebel commander Huang Ye at Xihua and stormed his encampment.

sentences.zh: 巢賊大恐，收軍營于故陽里，官軍進攻之。

translations.literal: Chao's rebels were greatly afraid; they gathered their army and encamped at old Yangli, and the government army pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao's forces were seized with terror. They pulled back to encamp at old Yangli, and the imperial army pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 五月，大雨震雷，平地水深三尺，壞賊壘，賊自離散，復聚于尉氏，逼中牟。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, great rain and thunder shook the heavens; water in the flat land was three feet deep, destroying the rebel fortifications; the rebels dispersed on their own, then gathered again at Weishi and pressed Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month torrential rains and thunder flooded the plain to a depth of three feet, wrecking the rebel fortifications. The army scattered, then regrouped at Weishi and threatened Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 翌日，營汴水北。

translations.literal: The next day they encamped north of the Bian River.
translations.idiomatic: The following day they encamped north of the Bian River.

sentences.zh: 是日，復大雨震電，溝塍漲流。

translations.literal: That day, again came great rain and thunder; ditches and field ridges overflowed in rushing streams.
translations.idiomatic: That same day another storm broke, and ditches and field embankments burst into rushing flood.

sentences.zh: 賊分寇汴州，李克用自鄭州引軍襲擊，大敗之，獲賊將李用、楊景。

translations.literal: The rebels divided their forces to raid Bianzhou; Li Keyong led his army from Zhengzhou in a surprise attack and greatly defeated them, capturing the rebel generals Li Yong and Yang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels split off a force to raid Bianzhou. Li Keyong marched from Zhengzhou, fell upon them by surprise, and won a great victory, capturing the rebel generals Li Yong and Yang Jing.

sentences.zh: 殘眾保胙縣、冤句，官軍追討，賊無所保。

translations.literal: The remnant host held Zuoxian and Yuanju; the government army pursued and attacked, and the rebels had nowhere to shelter.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors held out at Zuoxian and Yuanju, but the imperial army hunted them down until they had nowhere left to hide.

sentences.zh: 其將李讜、楊能、霍存、葛從周、張歸厚、張歸霸各率部下降于大梁，尚讓率部下萬人歸時薄。

translations.literal: Their generals Li Dan, Yang Neng, Huo Cun, Ge Congzhou, Zhang Guihou, and Zhang Guiba each led their commands in surrender to Daliang; Shang Rang led ten thousand men of his command in submission to Shi Pu.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders Li Dan, Yang Neng, Huo Cun, Ge Congzhou, Zhang Guihou, and Zhang Guiba each surrendered their units to Daliang; Shang Rang brought ten thousand of his men over to Shi Pu.

sentences.zh: 賊自相猜間，相殺于營中，所殘者千人，中夜遁去。

translations.literal: The rebels mutually suspected one another and killed one another in the camps; those who remained numbered a thousand; at midnight they fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicion turned the rebel camps inward; they fell upon one another until only a thousand remained, and at midnight they broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 克用追擊至濟陰而還。

translations.literal: Keyong pursued in attack to Jiyin and then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong pursued them as far as Jiyin, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賊散於兗、鄆界。

translations.literal: The rebels scattered on the border of Yan and Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant rebels scattered along the border of Yan and Yun.

sentences.zh: 黃巢入泰山，徐帥時薄遣將張友與尚讓之眾掩捕之。

translations.literal: Huang Chao entered Mount Tai; the commander of Xu, Shi Pu, dispatched the general Zhang You together with Shang Rang's host to lie in ambush and capture him.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao fled into Mount Tai. Shi Pu, military governor of Xuzhou, sent the general Zhang You with Shang Rang's troops to trap and seize him.

sentences.zh: 至狼虎穀，巢將林言斬巢及二弟鄴、揆等七人首，並妻子皆送徐州。

translations.literal: At Langhu Valley, Chao's general Lin Yan cut off the heads of Chao and his two younger brothers Ye and Kui and seven others altogether, and sent them together with their wives and children to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At Langhu Valley, Huang Chao's officer Lin Yan struck off the heads of Chao, his two brothers Ye and Kui, and five others—seven in all—and sent them with their wives and children to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是月賊平。

translations.literal: In that month the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That month the rebellion was brought to an end.

sentences.zh: 秦宗權

translations.literal: Qin Zongquan
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan

sentences.zh: 中和三年，巢賊走關東，宗權逆戰不利，因與合從為盜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhonghe, when Chao's rebels fled to the eastern passes, Zongquan met them in counter-battle with ill fortune and therefore joined them in league as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhonghe (883), when Huang Chao's forces fled east beyond the passes, Qin Zongquan fought them and met defeat; he then threw in his lot with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 巢賊既誅，宗權復熾，僭稱帝號，補署官吏。

translations.literal: After Chao's rebels were executed, Zongquan again flourished fiercely; he usurped an imperial title and appointed officials.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao's death Qin Zongquan rose up more violent than before: he declared himself emperor and installed a full roster of officials.

sentences.zh: 遣其將秦彥亂江淮，秦賢亂江南，秦誥陷襄陽，孫儒陷孟、洛、陝、虢至於長安，張眰陷汝、鄭，盧塘攻汴州。

translations.literal: He dispatched his generals Qin Yan to ravage the Jiang-Huai region, Qin Xian to ravage Jiangnan, Qin Gao to capture Xiangyang, Sun Ru to capture Meng, Luo, Shan, Guo, and as far as Chang'an, Zhang Zhi to capture Ru and Zheng, and Lu Tang to attack Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals on campaigns of ruin: Qin Yan ravaged the Jiang-Huai region; Qin Xian laid waste to Jiangnan; Qin Gao took Xiangyang; Sun Ru seized Meng, Luo, Shan, Guo, and pushed as far as Chang'an; Zhang Zhi overran Ru and Zheng; and Lu Tang attacked Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊首皆慓銳慘毒，所至屠殘人物，燔燒郡邑。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftains were all fierce, sharp, and cruelly poisonous; wherever they arrived they slaughtered and mutilated people and burned commanderies and districts.
translations.idiomatic: Every rebel leader was ruthless and savage; wherever they marched they butchered the populace and put towns to the torch.

sentences.zh: 西至關內，東極青、齊，南出江淮，北至衛滑，魚爛鳥散，人煙斷絕，荊榛蔽野。

translations.literal: West to the inner passes, east to the extremity of Qing and Qi, south out to the Jiang-Huai, north to Wei and Hua—fish rotted and birds scattered; human smoke ceased; thorns and brambles covered the wild fields.
translations.idiomatic: From the western heartland to the farthest reaches of Qing and Qi, from the Jiang-Huai south to Wei and Hua north, the land lay in ruin: populations vanished, hearth fires went dark, and wild thorns choked the abandoned fields.

sentences.zh: 賊既乏食，啖人為儲，軍士四出，則鹽屍而從。

translations.literal: When the rebels lacked food, they ate people for stores; when the soldiers went out on all sides, they carried salted corpses to follow them.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions ran short the rebels fed on human flesh laid up as rations; when columns marched out, they carried salted corpses in their train.

sentences.zh: 關東郡邑，多被攻陷。

translations.literal: Commanderies and districts of the eastern passes were mostly attacked and captured.
translations.idiomatic: City after city east of the passes fell to their assault.

sentences.zh: 唯趙犨兄弟守陳州，朱溫保汴州，城門之外，為賊疆場。

translations.literal: Only the brothers Zhao Chao held Chenzhou, and Zhu Wen held Bianzhou; beyond the city gates all was the rebels' battleground.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Zhao brothers held out at Chenzhou, and Zhu Wen held Bianzhou; beyond their city gates lay nothing but rebel territory.

sentences.zh: 汴帥與兗、鄆合勢，屢敗賊軍，凶勢日削。

translations.literal: The Bian commander, combining strength with Yan and Yun, repeatedly defeated the rebel army, and their fierce momentum daily waned.
translations.idiomatic: The military governor of Bian, allied with Yan and Yun, repeatedly defeated the rebel armies, and their power daily declined.

sentences.zh: 龍紀元年二月，其愛將申叢執宗權，撾折其足，送於汴。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Longji, his beloved general Shen Cong seized Zongquan, broke his legs with a cudgel, and sent him to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Longji (889), his favorite general Shen Cong seized Qin Zongquan, beat his legs until they broke, and sent him to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 朱溫出師迎勞，接之以禮。

translations.literal: Zhu Wen marched out his army to welcome and comfort him, receiving him with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen marched out to receive him with ceremony and courtesy.

sentences.zh: 謂之曰：「下官屢以天子命達于公，如前年中翻然改圖，與下官同力勤王，則豈有今日之事乎？」

translations.literal: He said to him: "Your subordinate has repeatedly conveyed the Son of Heaven's orders to you, sir; if as in the year before last you had suddenly changed your course and joined your subordinate in exerting strength to aid the royal house, how could there be today's affair?
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wen said to him: "I have carried the emperor's orders to you again and again. Had you, as in the year before last, turned back to join me in serving the throne, we would not be here today.

sentences.zh: 宗權曰：「僕若不死，公何以興？

translations.literal: Zongquan said: "If your servant did not die, how could you, sir, rise?
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan replied: "If I did not die, how could you rise?

sentences.zh: 天以僕霸公也。」

translations.literal: Heaven used your servant to make you, sir, a hegemon."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven used me to make you great."

sentences.zh: 略無懼色，乃檻送京師。

translations.literal: He showed not the least fear, and was sent to the capital in a caged cart.
translations.idiomatic: He showed not a trace of fear and was sent to the capital in a prisoner cart.

sentences.zh: 昭宗御延喜樓受俘，京兆尹孫揆以組練礫之，徇於兩市。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong received the captive at Yanxi Tower; the metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, Sun Kui, stoned him with cobbles bound in cord and paraded him through both markets.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong received the prisoner at Yanxi Tower. Sun Kui, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, had him pelted with stones bound in cord and paraded through both markets of the capital.

sentences.zh: 宗權檻中引頸謂揆曰：「尚書明鑒，宗權豈反者耶！

translations.literal: Zongquan in the cage stretched his neck and said to Kui: "Minister, with clear discernment—Zongquan is no rebel!
translations.idiomatic: From his cage Qin Zongquan craned his neck toward Sun Kui and cried: "Minister, judge clearly—I am no rebel!

sentences.zh: 但輸忠不效耳。」

translations.literal: I only failed in my loyal submission.
translations.idiomatic: I only failed in my loyal service.

sentences.zh: 眾大笑。

translations.literal: The crowd laughed loudly.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd roared with laughter.

sentences.zh: 與妻趙氏俱斬于獨柳之下。

translations.literal: Together with his wife Lady Zhao he was beheaded below Duliuyu.
translations.idiomatic: He and his wife Lady Zhao were beheaded below Duliuyu.

sentences.zh: 【評論】

translations.literal: Commentary
translations.idiomatic: Commentary

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：我唐之受命也，置器于安，千年惟永，百蠻響化，萬國來王。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: When our Tang received the Mandate, it set the vessel in peace; for a thousand years it was to endure, the hundred barbarians answered to transformation, and the myriad states came as kings.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When the Tang received Heaven's mandate, the vessel of state was set in peace; the realm was to endure a thousand years, the hundred barbarians were to be transformed, and ten thousand kingdoms were to pay homage.

sentences.zh: 但否泰之無恆，故夷險之不一。

translations.literal: But fortune and misfortune have no constancy, and so peril and ease are not one.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fortune and misfortune know no constancy, and safety and danger do not abide in one place.

sentences.zh: 三百算祀，二十帝王。

translations.literal: For three hundred calculated generations, twenty emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred years of reckoned reign, twenty emperors.

sentences.zh: 雖時有竊邑叛君之臣。

translations.literal: Though at times there were ministers who usurped districts and rebelled against their lords,
translations.idiomatic: Though from time to time there were men who seized territories and turned against their sovereigns,

sentences.zh: 乘危徼幸之輩，莫不才興兵革，即就誅夷。

translations.literal: and men who took advantage of crisis to grasp at luck, none failed to raise arms at once and promptly meet execution.
translations.idiomatic: and opportunists who seized on crisis for private gain, none failed to take up arms only to be swiftly put to death.

sentences.zh: 其間沸騰，大盜三發，安祿山、朱泚、黃巢是也。

translations.literal: Among them the three great bandits boiled up: An Lushan, Zhu Ci, and Huang Chao were such men.
translations.idiomatic: Among them three great rebels boiled up in succession: An Lushan, Zhu Ci, and Huang Chao.

sentences.zh: 夫謀危社稷，將害君親，轘裂瀦宮，未塞其罪，故不俟于多談也。

translations.literal: Those who plot peril to the altars of state and would harm the ruler and kin, who tear apart the imperial palace—no punishment can satisfy their crime; therefore they need not wait for lengthy discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Men who threatened the altars of state and would harm emperor and kin, who laid waste to the palace itself—their crimes admit no measure of punishment and need no lengthy debate.

sentences.zh: 然盜之所起，必有其來，且無問于天時，宜決之於人事。

translations.literal: Yet wherever banditry arises, it must have its source; setting aside the seasons of Heaven, the decision lies in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yet wherever rebellion arises it has its causes; leaving aside the workings of Heaven, the answer lies in what men do.

sentences.zh: 祿山母為巫者，身是牙郎，偶緣微立邊功，遂至大加寵用，總知馬牧，特委兵權。

translations.literal: Lushan's mother was a shaman; he himself was a broker in the markets; by chance he won minor frontier merit and came to receive great favor and employment, with overall charge of horse herds and special entrustment of military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan's mother was a shaman and he himself a petty broker; by chance he won minor merit on the frontier and was showered with favor, given charge of the horse herds and entrusted with military authority.

sentences.zh: 愛天子之獨尊，與國忠之相忌，故不能以義制事，以禮制心，遂稱向闕之兵，以期非望之福，此所以為亂也！

translations.literal: He loved the Son of Heaven's exclusive supremacy and was mutually jealous with Guozhong; therefore he could not restrain affairs by righteousness or restrain his heart by ritual, and so called his army one that marched toward the palace, hoping for unlooked-for fortune—this is why he made rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: He resented the emperor's sole supremacy and feuded with Yang Guozhong; he could not govern his conduct by righteousness or his heart by ritual. He marched on the capital in the name of loyalty while reaching for fortune beyond his due—that is why he rebelled.

sentences.zh: 朱泚家本漁陽，性惟凶狡，耳習聞於篡奪，心本之于忠貞。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's family was originally from Yuyang; his nature was only fierce and cunning; his ears were accustomed to hearing of usurpation, yet his heart was rooted in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's family came from Yuyang; his nature was fierce and cunning; his ears were filled with tales of usurpation, yet his heart was rooted in loyalty to the throne.

sentences.zh: 暨弟為亂階，身留京邑，小不如意，別懷異圖。

translations.literal: When his younger brother became the stair of rebellion and he himself remained in the capital, the least discontent stirred a different design in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother became the stepping-stone to rebellion and he remained at the capital, the smallest grievance bred treason in his mind.

sentences.zh: 但樂荒雞之鳴，唯幸和鑾之動，緣幽帥之嘗因亂得，謂神器之可以徼求。

translations.literal: He only delighted in the crow of the wild cock at dawn and only hoped for the movement of the imperial carriage; because the Youzhou commander had once gained power through rebellion, he supposed the sacred vessel could be sought by bold demand.
translations.idiomatic: He rejoiced at every rumor of unrest and prayed for the emperor's flight; because the Youzhou commanders had once won power through rebellion, he believed the throne itself could be seized by force.

sentences.zh: 黃巢亹茸微人，萑蒲賤類，因饑饉之歲，躡王、尚之蹤，志在奪攘，謀非遠大。

translations.literal: Huang Chao was a trifling, low-born man of the reeds and rushes; because in years of famine and dearth he followed in the tracks of Wang and Shang, his aim lay in seizure and plunder, and his design was not far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao was a nobody from the marshes and wastes; in years of famine he followed Wang Xianzhi and Shang Rang, bent on plunder rather than any grand design.

sentences.zh: 一旦長驅江表，徑入關中，見五輅之蒙塵，謂寶命之在我。

translations.literal: Once he drove at length through the lands south of the Yangzi and entered the central passes directly, seeing the five imperial carriages dust-covered, he supposed the precious mandate was his.
translations.idiomatic: When he swept through the south and drove straight into Guanzhong, seeing the imperial carriages in the dust, he believed the Mandate of Heaven was his.

sentences.zh: 必若玄宗采九齡之語，行三令之威，不然使祿山名位不高，委任得所，則群黎未必陷於塗炭，萬乘未必越於岷，峨。

translations.literal: Had Xuanzong taken Zhang Jiuling's counsel and exercised the awe of the three commands—or otherwise kept Lushan's rank and commission from growing too high and his trust properly placed—then the common people would not necessarily have fallen into charcoal and ash, and the Son of Heaven would not necessarily have crossed Min and E.
translations.idiomatic: Had Xuanzong heeded Zhang Jiuling and wielded the full authority of command—or had he kept Lushan's rank modest and his trust rightly placed—the people would not have been cast into ruin, and the emperor would not have fled beyond Min and E.

sentences.zh: 德宗能含垢匿瑕，不佳兵尚勇，不然則取李承之言，不委希烈伐叛，不然則取公輔之諫，早令朱泚就行，如此則未必有涇原之亂兵，未必有奉天之危急！

translations.literal: Had Dezong been able to swallow filth and hide flaws and not prize arms and valor—or otherwise taken Li Cheng's words and not entrusted Xilie with suppressing rebellion—or otherwise taken the remonstrance of the chief ministers and early ordered Zhu Ci to depart—then there would not necessarily have been the mutiny of the Jingyuan troops, nor necessarily the peril of Fengtian!
translations.idiomatic: Had Dezong borne insult without rash war—or heeded Li Cheng and not entrusted Li Xilie with the campaign—or taken his ministers' advice and sent Zhu Ci away in time—there might have been no Jingyuan mutiny and no desperate flight to Fengtian.

sentences.zh: 僖宗能知人疾苦，惠彼困窮，不然則從鄭畋之謀，赦群偷之罪，如此則黃巢不必能犯順，鑾禦未必須省方。

translations.literal: Had Xizong been able to know the people's suffering and show kindness to the distressed—or otherwise followed Zheng Tian's plan and pardoned the crimes of the bandit host—then Huang Chao would not necessarily have been able to violate submission, and the imperial carriage would not necessarily have had to remove to another region.
translations.idiomatic: Had Xizong understood the people's suffering and aided the destitute—or followed Zheng Tian and pardoned the rebel ranks—Huang Chao might never have marched on the capital, and the emperor might never have fled the realm.

sentences.zh: 蓋差之毫釐，失之千里。

translations.literal: A miss of a hair's breadth, and the error is a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: A hair's breadth of error, and the loss is a thousand li.

sentences.zh: 蛇螫不能斷腕，蟻穴所以壞堤。

translations.literal: A snake's sting cannot make one sever the wrist; an ant's hole is what ruins the dike.
translations.idiomatic: A serpent's bite will not make a man cut off his wrist; yet an anthill is enough to breach a dike.

sentences.zh: 後之帝王，足為殷鑒！

translations.literal: Later emperors and kings—let this suffice as a lesson drawn from Yin!
translations.idiomatic: Let later emperors take this as a warning carved in bronze.

sentences.zh: 史朝義、秦宗權乘彼亂離，肆行暴虐，虔劉我郡邑，僭竊我衣裳，終雖滅亡，為害斯甚，茲亦沴氣之餘也。

translations.literal: Shi Chaoyi and Qin Zongquan, riding those times of disorder and separation, ran rampant in cruelty; they slaughtered our commanderies and districts and usurped our robes and caps; though in the end they perished, the harm was very great—this too is the residue of baleful qi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chaoyi and Qin Zongquan exploited the chaos to run wild in cruelty, slaughtering our towns and donning our imperial robes; though they perished in the end, the harm they did was immense—another residue of the age's malignant air.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：天地否閉，反逆亂常。

translations.literal: Praise says: Heaven and earth are blocked and closed; rebels violate the constant order.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal runs: When heaven and earth fall out of harmony, rebels overturn the natural order.

sentences.zh: 祿山犯闕，朱泚稱皇。

translations.literal: Lushan violated the palace gates; Zhu Ci styled himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lushan stormed the palace; Zhu Ci declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 賊巢陵突，群豎披攘。

translations.literal: The bandit Chao stormed and burst through; the mob of villains was scattered and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao swept the realm; his rabble was broken and scattered.

sentences.zh: 征其所以，存乎慢藏！

translations.literal: Investigating what they sprang from—it lies in treating the storehouse with contempt!
translations.idiomatic: Seek the root of their rise, and it lies in contempt for what the storehouse holds dear.
